1: If in the explanations of all the prophets we need the coming of the Holy Spirit, so that they may be opened by the revelation of him by whose prompting they were written; and if in Isaiah and in the Apocalypse we read of a sealed book, which the scribes and Pharisees, who boast that they know the letters of the law, cannot read, because it is sealed, and no one could be found who could unlock its mysteries except the lion of the tribe of Judah, whom God the Father has sealed: how much more, in the explanation of the prophet Hosea, must the Lord be prayed to, and must we say with Peter: Explain this parable to us. Especially since he who wrote it himself testifies at the end to the obscurity of the volume: Who is wise, and he will understand these things, understanding, and he will know them? This we ought to take not as something impossible but as something difficult, according to that saying of the Gospel: Who, do you think, is the faithful and prudent servant whom the Lord has set over his household? For who would not at once, at the very front of the book, be scandalized and say: Hosea, first of all the prophets, is commanded to take a harlot as his wife, and he does not object? He does not even pretend to be unwilling, so as to seem to do a shameful thing against his will; but he carries out the command gladly, as though he had longed for it, as though he regretted having given himself to chastity for a long time; whereas we read that holy men, at the Lord's command, refused things more honorable and without sin. Moses is sent to Pharaoh and appointed leader of the Israelite people; and yet, not from weakness but from humility, he answered: Provide another whom you may send. Jeremiah says that he is a boy, so as not to rebuke Jerusalem in her sin. Ezekiel is commanded to make one loaf baked under the ashes from every kind of pulse and seed, and to cook it in human dung; and he says: By no means, Lord, for nothing unclean has ever entered my mouth. And Hosea, hearing from the Lord: Take a fornicating wife, does not knit his brow, does not testify to his grief by pallor, does not show his shame by a changed blush on his cheeks; but he goes to the brothel and leads the harlot to his bed. And he does not initiate her into the chastity of a matron; rather he proves himself a voluptuary and a profligate. For he who cleaves to a harlot becomes one body with her. Hearing these things, then, what can we answer except that prophetic word: Who is wise, and he will understand these things, understanding, and he will know them? Hence we too must say with David: Unveil my eyes, and I will consider the wonders of your law, so that the king may bring us into his chamber, and take away from us the veil which was placed before the eyes of Moses in the reading of the Old Testament. For as soon as the Lord had said: Father, into your hands I commend my spirit; and saying this he breathed his last, the veil of the temple was torn, and all the secrets of the Jews lay open. And the fountain that went forth from the house of David entered the sea of the wilderness; and the true Elisha seasoned the barren and deadly waters with the salt of his wisdom and made them life-giving. And the Marah of the law, which is interpreted bitterness, was sweetened by the wood of the gibbet. For we understand who Judah the patriarch is, chosen to be king, and we do not wonder why a holy man goes in to Tamar as to a harlot; why Samson, which is interpreted sun, loved Delilah, which is translated poor, and, mocked on her account and dying, slaughtered thousands of his adversaries; why Salmon begot the just man Boaz from Rahab the harlot, Boaz who, covering Ruth the Moabitess with the wing of his cloak, carried her over from lying at his feet to the head of the Gospel. What reason there is that, though David had so many wives, he made no other the successor of his kingdom except the one who was born of Bathsheba; so that not only harlots but even adulteresses seem to please God. Hence in this very prophet too we read that, joined first to a harlot, he is coupled secondly to an adulteress, the Lord saying to him: Go again, love a woman beloved of a friend, or loving evil things, and an adulteress. This is the woman, harlot and adulteress, who in the Gospel washed the Lord's feet with her tears, wiped them with her hair, and honored them with the ointment of her confession; and when the disciples were indignant, and above all the betrayer, that it had not been sold and its price distributed for the food of the poor, the Lord answered: Why do you trouble the woman? She has done a good work on me; the poor you will always have with you; but me you will not always have. And lest we should think what she had done a light thing, and that the pistic nard, that is, the most faithful ointment, was to be referred to something else and not to the Church, he gives us an occasion for understanding; and he promises great rewards to great faith, saying: Amen, amen I say to you, wherever this Gospel is preached in the whole world, what she too has done will be told in memory of her. This is the harlot of whom the Lord speaks to the Jews: Amen I say to you, harlots and publicans will go before you into the kingdom of God. For you were unwilling to receive the Son of the householder, the Lord of the vineyard, who planted it, when he was sent to you. This harlot received with kindness my two spies, most valiant young men, of whom I sent one to the circumcision and the other to the Gentiles; she hid them with zeal, lifted them up onto the roof, and covered them with stalks of flax. That flax, cut down by persecutions and washed in baptism, changes its color, and from dark is turned to white. Nor is it surprising if we recall that these things were done as a figure of the Lord Savior and of the Church gathered from sinners, since he himself says in this same prophet: I will speak to the prophets; I have multiplied visions, and in the hands of the prophets I have been likened; so that whatever the prophets are commanded to do is to be referred to my likeness. His wife is an Ethiopian, against whom Aaron and Mary, the carnal priesthood of the Jews and the prophecy that serves the letter, murmur and offend God; she it is who says in the Song of Songs: I am dark and beautiful, daughters of Jerusalem. Otherwise, if we contend that all the things which are commanded for a reason, to be done as a likeness, really happened, then Jeremiah too, girded with a loincloth, a woman's garment, went among innumerable nations, the Assyrians and the Chaldeans, the peoples most hostile to the Jews, to the Euphrates, and there hid his loincloth, and, returning after a long time, found that it had rotted so as to be of no use. How could he go out and travel so far when Jerusalem was besieged, with siege works built all around it, ditch, rampart and forts? He who, when he once wished to go out to Anathoth, his little village situated at the third milestone from the city, was both seized at the gate and led back to the princes, and, beaten as a traitor, was thrown into prison. If that was in figure, because it could not happen, then this too is in figure, because if it happened, it would be most shameful. But you will answer: When God commands, nothing is shameful; and we will say: God commands nothing except what is honorable, nor by commanding shameful things does he make honorable what is shameful. But because we know that God wills nothing except what is honorable, he commanded this, which is honorable. I have spoken of these things at greater length at the beginning, so as first to solve the most difficult question, and, passing with God's help the rock set in the very mouth of the passage, to run down into safe waters. For the rest, I am not unaware, dearest Pammachius, that it has been passed over by many churchmen; and of those who attempted to expound it, among the Greeks I found Apollinaris of Laodicea, who, though in his youth he had left brief little commentaries both on this prophet and on others, touching the senses rather than unfolding them, was asked afterwards to write more fully on Hosea; that book has come into our hands, but he too, through excessive brevity, cannot lead the reader to a perfect understanding. Origen wrote a small book on this prophet, to which he gave this title: Περὶ τοῦ πῶς ὠνομάσθη ἐν τῷ Ὠσηὲ Ἐφραΐμ; that is: Why Ephraim is so called in Hosea, wishing to show that whatever is said against him is to be referred to the person of the heretics. And another volume, ἀκέφαλον καὶ ἀτέλεστον, which lacks both head and end. I have also read a very long treatise of Pierius, which he poured out on the opening of this prophet on the day of the vigil of the Lord's passion, in an extempore and eloquent discourse. And Eusebius of Caesarea, in the eighteenth book of the Εὐαγγελικῆς ἀποδείξεως (the Demonstration of the Gospel), discusses certain matters concerning the prophet Hosea. Hence about twenty-two years ago, when, at the request of your holy and venerable mother-in-law, or rather your mother, Paula (for the one is the name of the flesh, the other of the spirit; she always burned with love for monasteries and for the Scriptures), I was at Alexandria, I saw Didymus, the most learned man of his time, and heard him often; and I asked him to complete what Origen had not done, and to write commentaries on Hosea; and he dictated three books to me, at my request, and five others also on Zechariah. For on that prophet too Origen wrote only two volumes, expounding barely a third part, from the beginning of the book up to the vision of the four-horse chariots. I say these things so that you may know whom I have had as forerunners in the field of this prophet; whom, however, to confess it to your prudence simply and not proudly — as a certain one of my friends is always hissing — I have not followed in everything; so that I might be a judge of their work rather than its translator, and might say what seemed right to me on each point, and what I received from the teachers of the Hebrews, barely one or two of them. Such a one is now a rare bird even among themselves, since all devote themselves to pleasures and money, and take more care of the belly than of the breast; and they think themselves learned in this, if in the shops of physicians they disparage the works of everyone. But now it is time that, setting down the words of the prophet, we discuss what is written.

The word of the Lord which came to Hosea son of Beeri. LXX: likewise. The Word of the Lord (which in the beginning was with God the Father, and the Word was God) came to Hosea son of Beeri, so as to make the prophet too a god, as the Savior says: If he called them gods to whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken, him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world you tell: You blaspheme; because I said, I am the Son of God. So that, just as God makes gods, and stands in the synagogue of gods, and in the midst he judges between gods; and, though he himself is the true light, which enlightens every man coming into this world, says to the apostles: You are the light of the world, so too the Savior himself may make his prophet a savior. For Hosea, in our language, means savior, a name which Joshua son of Nun also had before his name was changed by God. For he was not called — as is wrongly read in the Greek and Latin manuscripts — Ause, which means nothing at all; but Hoshea, that is, savior; and Lord was added to his name, so that he might be called savior of the Lord. This savior, then, is the son of Beeri, that is, of my well; such wells Abraham, Isaac and Jacob dug, and the foreigners were always trying to fill them in. Between a well and a pit, that is, a cistern, there is this difference: a well has perpetual waters, flowing from a living spring; a cistern, which keeps water cool, holds waters that are external and brought in from outside. Hence God speaks through the prophet Jeremiah: They have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and dug for themselves cisterns which cannot hold water. Of this fountain the psalmist cries out to God: With you is the fountain of life; in your light we shall see light. Hence some think that Beeri is interpreted my light; but the former is the true translation.

In the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, kings of Judah; and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel. LXX: likewise. Azariah, who is also called Uzziah, of the stock of David, reigned in Jerusalem over the two tribes, which were called Judah, for fifty-two years; his son Jotham succeeded him in the kingdom, and he too reigned for sixteen years; after him his son Ahaz reigned, likewise for sixteen years. After Ahaz his son Hezekiah reigned for twenty-nine years, in whose sixth year the ten tribes, which were called Israel, were captured by Shalmaneser king of the Chaldeans and settled in the mountains of the Medes. From this it is evident that, while Hosea, Isaiah and Joel, and Amos and Obadiah, and Jonah and Micah were prophesying, who were his σύγχρονοι (contemporaries), the kingdom of the ten tribes came to an end, which from the first king, Jeroboam, to the last, Hoshea, lasted two hundred and fifty years. At the time when Uzziah began to reign over Judah, Jeroboam, the great-grandson of Jehu, was reigning over Israel, Jehu to whom the Lord had promised that his offspring would reign to the fourth generation, because he had struck down the two impious kings of Judah and of Israel. We say this to show you briefly that the prophet Hosea prophesied both before the captivity of Israel and after its captivity, and that, treating it as near as well as present and past, he both announced it as coming, and mourned it as it fell upon them, and, for the correction of Judah, went back over it once past; and this we shall try to prove in the prophet himself according to the history. Uzziah is interpreted strength of the Lord; Jotham, consummation and perfection of the Lord; Ahaz, power; Hezekiah, command of the Lord. These reigned among the people of Judah, whose name is confession. Moreover, in Israel, which had made idols for itself and had been separated from the people of God, reigned Jeroboam son of Joash, which is interpreted χρονισμός, that is, temporality, or delay; because he loved the world and thought that to linger long in it was eternal life, delighting not at all in things to come but in things present.

It is asked why Ezekiel refused easier things, while Hosea was at once joined to a harlot and did not object, or rather reply, that he had a chaste body and ought not to be stained by union with a prostitute, as the Apostle says: He who cleaves to a prostitute becomes one body with her; from this it is shown that it was a figure of the Synagogue or of the Church, not truly carried out according to the letter, as we discussed more fully when expounding that prophet himself.

The beginning of the Lord's speaking in Hosea. LXX: The beginning of the word of the Lord to Hosea. Because, as we said above, Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, in whose reigns they prophesied, are set at the head of the title of other prophets too, he therefore now says that among all these the Lord spoke first in Hosea, and afterwards to the rest. But it is one thing for the Lord to speak in Hosea, another to speak to Hosea. In Hosea, he does not speak to Hosea himself, but through Hosea to others; but when he speaks to Hosea, he is signified to address his discourse to Hosea himself. Others, however, do not want Hosea to have been the first of all the prophets on the ground of what is said: The beginning of the Lord's speaking in Hosea; but hold that it shows that the Lord spoke these things which follow first to Hosea.

And the Lord said to Hosea: Go, take for yourself a wife of fornications and children of fornications, for the land, fornicating, will commit fornication away from the Lord. LXX: And the Lord said to Hosea: Go, take for yourself a wife of fornication and children of fornication, for the land, fornicating, will commit fornication behind the Lord. The Hebrew word zanunim means not a fornicating woman and fornication, as most suppose, but many fornications. From this it is shown that this woman, whom the prophet takes in marriage, had committed fornication not once but quite often, so that the more sordid she is, the more patient is the prophet who married such a wife. And as for what is added: Take for yourself also children of fornications; for it is understood ἀπὸ κοινοῦ (from what is common, i.e. understood with both parts): Take for yourself a wife of fornications, and take for yourself children of fornications. Both can be understood: that he both receives the children whom the fornicating woman had earlier conceived from fornication, and himself begets offspring from the harlot, who are therefore to be called children of fornication, because they were begotten of a harlot. Nor is the prophet to be blamed, to follow the history for the moment, if he converted a harlot to chastity, but rather praised, because he made a good woman out of a bad one. For he who remains good is not himself polluted if he is joined to one who is bad; but he who is bad is turned to good if he follows the examples of the good. From this we understand that the prophet did not lose his chastity by being joined to a fornicating woman, but that the fornicating woman took on the chastity which she did not have before; especially since blessed Hosea did not act for the sake of luxury, nor of lust, nor of his own will, but obeyed the command of God, so that what we read done carnally in him we might show to have been done spiritually in God, who took to himself the Synagogue, that is, the people of the Jews, enslaved to fornication and lust. To her the Lord speaks through Ezekiel: And you, harlot, hear the word of the Lord. For her breasts were broken in Egypt, and she was wallowing in blood, and had been polluted up to the crown of her head, so that there was no part of her body and limbs which did not bear the stain of shame. Such a woman the Lord covered with his cloak and joined to his embraces; he gave her honey and oil and fine flour to eat, and clothed her in the most precious garments; he placed ornaments of gems on her neck; he adorned her ears with gold and most precious stone; he also furnished bracelets for her arms, so that she might practice good works. And nevertheless, despising this generosity and goodness of her husband, forgetful of her former shame, she followed her lovers, the Chaldeans and Assyrians and Egyptians, who are of great flesh. Of the type of the Savior and the Church we spoke in the little preface: that he took for himself a fornicating wife, who previously served idols. But if anyone contentious, and especially of the Gentiles, refuses to accept that it is said figuratively, and mocks the prophet for being joined to a fornicating woman, let us set against him what Greece is wont to praise and the schools of the philosophers sing in chorus. On what ground do they extol that most learned man Xenocrates, who made Polemon, a most dissolute youth, drunk and crowned with ivy among harp-girls and pipers and shameless women, obey wisdom, and changed a most shameful young man into the wisest of philosophers? Why do they raise Socrates to heaven, who transferred Phaedo, after whose name a book of Plato is called, from a brothel, where through the cruelty and avarice of his master he served the lust of many, into the Academy? And whatever they answer about these masters of philosophy, we apply to the defense of the prophet. Let this be said against the heathen and those who are like the heathen. But to our own, who nevertheless wish to accept the truth, let us briefly show this, from what is said: For the land, fornicating, will commit fornication away from the Lord: that it is not so much that the prophet was joined to a harlot as that the whole human race withdrew from fellowship with the Lord. Also, since "all the earth" is not added, it can be taken here as Judea, or properly Samaria and Israel, that is, the ten tribes, which, at the time when these things were being said, had withdrawn from the Lord.

By the law the prophet was allowed to take a woman into the marriage relationship, and on marrying her he probably brought her to chaste ways. In fact, while everyone could not but be surprised that a man who was very conscious of propriety should pass over women who enjoyed a good reputation and choose to take a prostitute into the marriage relationship, the novelty of the event provided the prophet with the occasion of telling them their duty. In addition [Hosea's marriage demonstrated] the greater marvel of God's condescending to choose such ungrateful people for special attention by the powerful example—namely, the remarkable prophet's doing his duty by entering into association with a prostitute.

Likewise the Lord of all had bade Hosea also, therefore, marry a loose woman so as by the event to charge the people with impiety and give evidence of his characteristic longsuffering. If the God of all put up with the loose and adulterous synagogue, however, and the fount of holiness was not defiled by that loathsome and abominable thing, neither did the prophet incur any defilement from that licentious woman. Without being in thrall to lust, and instead carrying out a command from on high, he put up with that awful relationship. Now one must realize how judgment is made between good and bad by the purpose involved: on that basis marriage is distinguished from adultery, and though intercourse involves no difference, the difference emerges in the purpose and the law, and on the same basis what is lawful is distinguished from what is lawless.

Against conjugal chastity it is objected: every act and movement that alienates from God is foreign to virtue: but the act of conjugal continence is such: therefore it is foreign to virtue. Proof of the middle term: Hosea 1; the Gloss: "Just as wine intoxicates a man and alienates him from the state of his mind, so the law of marriage alienates a man from the things that are of God."

To this it must be said that something is said to alienate from God in two ways: either simply, or with respect to some act or state. In the first way it cannot be without sin: in the second way it can be through the punishment of sin and also through an act of virtue: just as the exercise of action retards and for a time impedes the act of contemplation, just as also sleep impedes the exercise in virtue.
Disputed Questions on Evangelical Perfection, Question 3

And he went and took Gomer daughter of Diblaim; and she conceived and bore him a son. And the Lord said to him: Call his name Jezreel, for yet a little while and I will visit the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu; and I will cause the kingdom of the house of Israel to cease. LXX: And he went, and took Gomer daughter of Diblaim; and she conceived and bore a son. And the Lord said to him: Call his name Jezreel, because yet a little while and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Judah; and I will cause the kingdom of the house of Israel to cease. The prophets make their promises about the coming of Christ and the calling of the Gentiles many ages later in such a way as not to neglect the present time, lest they seem not to teach an assembly called together for another purpose about the things that are at hand, but to trifle about things uncertain and future. And so this Gomer too, daughter of Diblaim, who is taken as wife by Hosea, and conceives by him, and bears him a son named Jezreel, which is interpreted seed of God, in vengeance for whose blood he overturns the kingdom of Jehu (or, as an error has wrongly prevailed, of Judah), is to be referred to the calling of the nations in such a way as to fit that time in which she is recorded to have borne a son. And not to keep the reader's eagerness waiting with a long treatment: these two women, of whom one is called Gomer and is a harlot, and bears three children, first Jezreel, second, a girl, who is called: Without Mercy, and third a male, who is himself also called: Not My People; and the other woman, who is hired for fifteen pieces of silver, and a cor, and half a cor of barley, and is called an adulteress, are referred to Israel and to Judah, that is, to the ten tribes which were in Samaria under king Jeroboam, who was of Ephraim, and to Judah, which reigned in Jerusalem from the stock of David. These are the two women who in Zechariah are said to have the wings of a hoopoe, or of a kite, or of a heron, and to go into the land of Shinar, where Babylon was founded. These women Oholah and Oholibah signify under the name of two sisters; these are shown in the two rods which Ezekiel joins into one rod. And because we are writing commentaries, not broad volumes, reserving for each section its own explanation in its place, let us now discuss only the present section.

Gomer is interpreted τετελεσμένην, that is, consummated and perfected; others think that θώρακας, that is, breastplates, is signified. There are some who suppose it means measure, or bitterness, which they would say rightly if it did not have the letter gimel. Diblaim means παλάτας (cakes of pressed figs), of which there is a very great abundance in Palestine, and which the prophet Isaiah is commanded to apply to the ulcer of king Hezekiah. It is a mass of rich dried figs, which they shape after the manner of bricks, tread and press together, so that they may remain long unspoiled.

Therefore Israel too, consummated and perfected in fornication, a daughter of pleasure, which seems sweet and pleasant to those who enjoy it, is taken as wife by Hosea as a type of the Lord Savior; and from her a son of God is first begotten, that is, Jezreel; and this is the metropolis of the ten tribes, in which Naboth was killed, on account of whose blood Jehu is raised up, who destroyed the house of Ahab and Jezebel. But because Jehu himself too, the avenger of just blood, walked in the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel commit fornication and set up golden calves in Dan and Bethel, his kingdom too is said to be overturned; under his great-grandson Jeroboam Hosea began to prophesy; when he died, his son Zechariah succeeded to the kingdom; and in the sixth month of his rule Shallum, born of another stock, killed him. For this reason it is now said: Yet a little while and I will visit the blood of Jezreel, that is, the slaughter of my people, upon the royal house of Jehu, which at that time ruled over Israel. Nor is it surprising if the house of Jehu is overturned, since even the kingdom of the house of Israel, that is, of the ten tribes, was to be utterly destroyed after not many years. For from Zechariah son of Jeroboam, whose ancestor was Jehu, to the ninth year of Hoshea, under whom the ten tribes were led into captivity, forty-nine years are counted. And once Zechariah, who was the last of the stock of Jehu, was killed, the kings of Assyria at once took Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh, which were beyond the Jordan; and then many cities of Samaria, and then all Naphtali, and at the last all the remaining tribes. In place of Jehu, in the common edition Judah is read; but this seems to me to have grown up not through the fault of the Seventy translators but through the ignorance of the copyists, who, not knowing Jehu, wrote Judah, which was more familiar. The type of the seed of God, and the vengeance for his blood, is referred to the Lord's passion, on account of which both the house of Judah and the kingdom of all Israel are said to be overturned.

And on that day I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel. LXX: likewise. When I have avenged the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and have destroyed the kingdom of Israel through the victory of the Assyrian, then on that day and at that time I will break all the strength of the army of Israel in the valley of Jezreel. We said above that Jezreel, which is now near Maximianopolis, was the metropolis of the kingdom of Samaria; near it are very broad plains, and a valley of exceeding vastness, which stretches for more than ten thousand paces. In this valley, when battle was joined, Israel was cut down by the Assyrians, that is, the ten tribes, which, on account of Jeroboam of the tribe of Ephraim, who first made a schism among the people, were called Ephraim. Sometimes, on account of Joseph, who was the father of Ephraim, it is called Joseph; sometimes Samaria, which was itself the other metropolitan city of the ten tribes, and which was afterwards called Augusta by Augustus Caesar, that is, Σεβαστὴ; in it the bones of John the Baptist are laid to rest. After the division, then, of the two and the ten tribes, because of the very great part of the multitude which followed Jeroboam, the ancient name Israel remained with the ten tribes. And on account of the tribe of Judah, which reigned in Jerusalem, the other tribes were called Judah; and at the same time the truth of the type is also unfolded. For just as, on account of the blood of Naboth, which was shed in Jezreel, the house of Ahab was destroyed, so that the prophecy of Elijah might be fulfilled; so, on account of the blood of the true Jezreel, that is, of the seed of God, the kingdom of the Jews was destroyed. In all the prophets indeed, but especially in Hosea, the ten tribes are referred to the heretics, whose multitude is very great; but the two tribes, which are called Judah, hold the person of the Church, and reign under the stock of David. The bow of the heretics, therefore, of whom it is written: The sons of Ephraim, bending and shooting the bow, turned back in the day of battle, will be broken in the valley of the seed of God, about whom they held lowly and earthly opinions.

According to the type, we say that those who, on account of the blood of the seed of God, are called: Without Mercy, and dared to say: His blood be upon us, and upon our children, serve the Romans to this day; but that the house of Judah, namely those of the Jews who confessed the Lord, were saved not by the strength of an army but by the preaching of the Gospel. What we have interpreted of Israel and Judah, both according to the history and according to the type, let us refer to the conventicles of the heretics and to the Church of the Lord Savior: that, while they are left without mercy and lose their kingdom, the Church has prevailed by the power of her God.

For οὐκ ἠλεημένη, that is, without mercy, in some copies is found οὐκ ἠγαπημένη, that is, not beloved. But the truer copies are those which have without mercy; especially since, to distinguish it from Israel, on whom he has no mercy, God adds: But on the house of Judah I will have mercy.

And she conceived again and bore a daughter; and he said to him: Call her name: Without Mercy; for I will no more have mercy on the house of Israel, but with forgetting I will forget them. And on the house of Judah I will have mercy; and I will save them in the Lord their God; and I will not save them by bow and sword, and by war, and by horses, and by horsemen. LXX: And she conceived again and bore a daughter, and he said to him: Call her name: Without Mercy; for by no means will I any more have mercy on the house of Israel, but opposing I will oppose them; but on the sons of Judah I will have mercy, and I will save them in the Lord their God; and I will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by war, nor by horses, nor by horsemen. After the bow of Israel was crushed and broken in the valley of Jezreel, and the kingdom of the ten tribes was forsaken, so that they were led into captivity, there is no longer born a Jezreel, that is, the seed of God, nor a son of the male sex; but a daughter, that is, a woman, of the frail sex, and one exposed to the insults of the victors; and she is called: Without Mercy. For she was led away captive for this reason, because she did not have the mercy of God. And the indignation of the Lord must be considered, in that he says he will by no means have mercy any more on the house of Israel, but will blot them out of his memory with an eternal forgetting; for to this day they serve the kings of the Persians, and their captivity has never been released.

Why, then, should we hesitate to say what Scripture does not shrink from declaring? Why shall the truth of faith hesitate in that wherein the authority of Scripture has never hesitated? For, behold, Hosea the prophet says in the person of the Father: "I will not now save them by bow, nor by horses, nor by horsemen; but I will save them by the Lord their God." If God says that He saves by God, still God does not save except by Christ. Why, then, should man hesitate to call Christ God, when he observes that He is declared to be God by the Father according to the Scriptures? Yea, if God the Father does not save except by God, no one can be saved by God the Father unless he shall have confessed Christ to be God, in whom and by whom the Father promises that He will give him salvation: so that, reasonably, whoever acknowledges Him to be God, may find salvation in Christ God; whoever does not acknowledge Him to be God, would lose salvation which he could not find elsewhere than in Christ God.

For He says to Hosea the prophet, "I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel, but will altogether be their enemy. But I will have mercy upon the children of Judah, and will save them in the Lord their God." Here God the Father gives the name of God, without any ambiguity, to the Son, in Whom also He chose us before countless ages. "Their God," He says, for while the Father, being Unoriginate, is independent of all, He has given us for an inheritance to His Son. In like manner we read, "Ask of Me, and I will give Thee the Gentiles for Thine inheritance." None can be God to Him from Whom are all things, for He is eternal and has no beginning; but the Son has God, from Whom He was born, for His Father. Yet to us the Father is God and the Son is God; the Father reveals to us that the Son is our God, and the Son teaches that the Father is God over us. The point for us to remember is that in this passage the Father gives to the Son the name of God, the title of His own unoriginate majesty.

But to the house of Judah he promises mercy, and says that he saves them in the Lord their God, either in himself who speaks; or the Father saves in the Son, according to what is written: The Lord rained from the Lord. For when Israel was handed over to the Assyrians, he saved them from the hand of Sennacherib, not by bow and sword and war and by a multitude of horsemen, but by his own strength, when he sent an angel and struck down from the army of Sennacherib king of the Assyrians in one night one hundred and eighty-five thousand.

And she weaned her who was Without Mercy; and she conceived and bore a son; and he said: Call his name Not My People, for you are not my people and I will not be yours. LXX: likewise. He who was called the seed of God, turned into a female and, because of the weakness of his strength and the offense of God, led into captivity, since he did not have the mercy of the Lord, is said to have been weaned not as a son but as a daughter; for the man had already lost his vigor. Whoever is weaned withdraws from the mother, no longer feeds on the parent's milk, and is sustained by food from outside. So also Israel, cast off by the Lord, hemmed in by the straits of captivity, and in Babylon sustained by unclean foods, is called not the people of God, and is struck with the eternal sentence of a foreign nation, so that he is called Not My People and is disowned forever. This we can rightly understand both of the whole people of the Jews, which, handed over to captivity because of the offense against the seed of God, lost its kingdom and its province and is called not the people of God, and also in the person of the heretics. But if some contentious interpreter will not accept what we have said, but understands that the harlot named Gomer, daughter of Diblaim, bore the first and the third as males and the second, the middle one, as a female, wanting the Scripture to mean just what is read, let him answer how he explains that passage in Ezekiel where he is commanded by the Lord to bear the iniquities of the house of Israel, that is, of the ten tribes, and for three hundred and ninety days to sleep continually on one side, the left, although in the LXX one hundred and ninety are written, and to sleep so that he never wakes nor changes his side, unless perhaps, sated with sleep, he opened his eyes a little to take the most filthy food of ash-baked bread, made of wheat and barley, and bean and lentil and millet, and baked on human dung. For the nature of things does not allow that any man should sleep always on one side for three hundred and ninety days. And again he says: You shall take up the iniquities of the house of Judah, and for forty days you shall sleep on the right side. These days, however, will be reckoned as years, during which Israel and Judah will be pressed down by siege and a very long captivity, so that, conquered and motionless, they cannot turn themselves from one side to the other. If he cannot prove that these things, and others like them which we read in the holy Scriptures, were done, but contends that they signify something else, then this harlot woman too, and the other woman, the adulteress, who were either joined to the prophet or kept by the prophet, indicate not a shameful union of lust but the mysteries of things to come.

Finally, whoever wishes fuller proof that mere words are nothing without actions should consider how countless peoples, by failing in good works, have lost the names given them. The twelve tribes of the Hebrews, when they were of old chosen by God, received two holy names, for they were called the people of God, and Israel. We read: "Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against thee." Once the Jews bore both these titles, now they have neither. They who long since left off the worship of God cannot be called God's people, nor can they who denied his Son be given a name that means "Seeing God." So it is written: "But Israel does not know, my people doth not consider."

For this reason on another occasion our God spoke of the people of the Hebrews to the prophet, saying: "Call his name, Not Beloved." And speaking to the Jews themselves: "You are not my people and I am not your God." Moreover, he himself showed clearly why he spoke thus about them, for he said: "They have forsaken the Lord, the fountain of living waters." And again: "They have rejected the word of the Lord and there is no wisdom in them."
On the Government of God, Book 4, Chapter 1

Thou wilt say then unto me, Why doth he yet find fault? For who hath resisted his will?  Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?  Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?  What if God, willing to show his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction:  And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory,  Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?  As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved.  And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God. [Hosea 1:10] Esaias also crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved:  For he will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness: because a short work will the Lord make upon the earth.  And as Esaias said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha.

And the number of the sons of Israel will be like the sand of the sea, which is without measure and will not be numbered. And it will be in the place where it will be said to them: You are not my people, it will be said to them: Sons of the living God. And the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel will be gathered together; and they will set over themselves one head and will go up from the land, for great is the day of Jezreel. LXX: And the number of the sons of Israel will be as the sand of the sea, which will not be measured nor can be numbered. And it will be in the place where it was said to them: You are not my people, they will be called sons of the living God. And the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel will be gathered together; and they will set over themselves one rule, and will go up from the land, for great is the day of Jezreel. We have read of the casting off of the ten tribes, and of Israel, not to be measured and no longer the people of God, condemned by perpetual indignation. Now we learn how the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel are gathered together, and set over themselves one head or rule; and go up from the land, and in the place where it was formerly said: Not my people, are called sons of the living God; and that this happens because great is the day of Jezreel. To one who is in doubt and wavering among various opinions there comes to mind that passage of Paul the Apostle writing to the Romans: What if God, wishing to show his wrath and to make known his power, endured with much patience the vessels of wrath fitted for destruction, so that he might show the riches of his glory upon the vessels of mercy which he prepared for glory; us whom he also called, not only from the Jews but also from the Gentiles, as he says in Hosea: I called not my people, my people, and: Not Obtained Mercy, Obtained Mercy. And it will be in the place where it was said to them: Not my people are you, there they will be called sons of the living God. But Isaiah cries out on behalf of Israel: If the number of the sons of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant will be saved. For he is completing and cutting short the word in equity, because the Lord will make a shortened word upon the earth. And as Isaiah foretold: Unless the Lord Sabaoth had left us a seed, we would have become like Sodom, and we would have been like Gomorrah. What then shall we say? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have laid hold of righteousness, but the righteousness that is from faith; but Israel, pursuing a law of righteousness, has not attained to the law of righteousness. Therefore the blessed Apostle, taking up the testimony of the prophet Hosea and expounding it of the calling of the Gentiles and of the faith of those of the Jews who were willing to believe, has cut away for us every difficulty of interpretation, asserting that it was fulfilled in the times of Christ; namely, that in Israel the twelve tribes are chosen, that is, the whole people of the Jews, and in Judah those of the Gentiles who confess the rule of the Lord. But if someone who is a stranger to the faith of Christ and does not accept the authority of the New Testament, but is of the number of the circumcision, replies that the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel denote the two tribes and the ten, of which we have often spoken, then, yielding even on this point, we will show that it does no harm to our faith. But after the number of the sons of Israel has been scattered like the sand of the sea throughout the whole world, and the multitude of the people has surpassed all reckoning, then Israel, who is a captive even today, and who was formerly called Without Mercy and Not My People, will have leave to enter into concord with the two tribes, that is, Judah and Benjamin, a great part of which believed in Christ, so that faith may join those who are separated in body, and they may set over themselves one head and prince; of whom Ezekiel wrote: And one prince in their midst, David my servant, and the dead will be raised as from hell, namely Judah and Israel, who were dead in unbelief. And all these things will come to pass because great is the day of the seed of God, which is interpreted as Christ. From this it is plain that the blood of Naboth the Jezreelite went before as a type precisely so that the truth might be fulfilled in Christ. For it is in him and not in the other that great is the day of Jezreel, of which it is said: This is the day which the Lord has made: let us exult and rejoice in it. Of the third interpretation which we have undertaken, explaining Israel as the heretics and Judah as the men of the Church, this is the sense: that after the Lord has come in his glory to reign, those who were formerly called not his people will be called sons of the living God, when they have been united to Judah, that is, to the Church of God, and have had one head, Christ, and have gone up from the land, that is, from earthly senses and the lowliness of the letter, and have taken up the great day of the seed of God.

Because Hosea is such a profound prophet, it is no easy matter to get at his meaning. Still, I must keep my promise and quote something from him at this point. He says, "And it shall be in the place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people'; it shall be said to them, 'You are sons of the living God.' " The apostles themselves understood this text as a prophecy of the calling of the Gentiles, who were previously not God's people. And because the Gentiles are spiritually sons of Abraham and correctly therefore alluded to as Israel, Hosea goes on to say, "And the children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together, and they shall appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the earth." Now to add one word of explanation to this text would be to lose the savor of Hosea's prophetic style.

"They come up out of the land," namely, they will live the life of the saints as well, "for great is the day of Jezreel." Indeed, great is the day of Christ, when he will raise to life all the dead. In fact, he will descend from heaven and sit on his glorious throne. "And he will give everyone according to his works." Therefore if one wishes to understand by "day" the time of the visitation—when the remission of sins is given by Christ to the Greeks, the Judaeans and those who have sinned against him—this will not deviate from the true words. For David too indicated the time of the coming of our Savior by saying, "This is the day that the Lord has made; let us be glad and rejoice in it."
2: Say to your brothers: My People, and to your sister: Obtained Mercy. LXX: Say to your brother: My People, and to your sister: Obtained Mercy. Since great is the day of Jezreel, in which Judah and Israel had one prince, and it will by no means be said to Israel: Not My People; but on the contrary they will be called sons of the living God. Therefore, O men of the tribe of Judah, do not despair of the salvation of the ten tribes, but daily, by word and by prayer and by letters, call them to repentance, because he is called your brother and your sister: brother from the fact that he is called My People; sister from the fact that he is named Obtained Mercy. Otherwise: you who believe in Christ, and are as much from the Jews as from the Gentiles, say to the broken branches, and to the former people which was cast off: My People, because he is your brother; and Obtained Mercy, because she is your sister. For when the fullness of the Gentiles has come in, then all Israel will be saved. This same thing is commanded us, that we should not utterly despair of the heretics, but call them to repentance, and desire their salvation with the affection of kinship.

The Synagogue is both of these, and if she persists in fornication and adultery, God will take away from her the garments and ornaments which he had given. Of these Ezekiel writes: On the day when you were born, they did not bind your breasts, and you were not salted with salt: and I passed by you, and found you naked, and disfigured, and spattered with blood. And a little after: I clothed you with fine linen and delicate stuffs, and placed ornaments about you, and gave bracelets about your hands, a necklace about your neck. These things her most generous husband gave her then, when he found her in Egypt, defiled by the lust of idolatry and spreading her feet for all. And now he threatens that, if she will not return to her husband, she will be without God and husband, just as she had been before in Egypt. Lest we always stretch out our volumes with a threefold explanation, let it suffice to have pointed this out now and then: that what has been said fits both the Jews who deny Christ and the heretics who abandon the faith of the Lord, whose fornication is properly between the breasts; and it dwells in the heart, in the craft of idols and of various dogmas; they will return to the day of their birth, so that, if they do not repent, they will be compared to the heathen.

Judge your mother, judge, since she is not my wife and I am not her husband; let her put away her fornications from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts, lest perhaps I strip her naked and set her as on the day of her birth. LXX: Be judged with your mother, be judged, because she is not my wife and I am not her husband; and I will put away her fornication from my face, and her adulteries from between her breasts, so that I may strip her naked, and restore her as on the day of her birth. Up to this point the discourse has been directed to the people of Israel, that is, to the ten tribes. Now another section begins, and the sons, that is, the people, are commanded to enter into judgment against their mother, who bore them, who, made a wife from a harlot, did not abandon her former ways, and again played the harlot with her lovers. And see the clemency of the husband. She has already been repudiated, already cast off; he has already said to her: She is not my wife and I am not her husband; yet he commands the sons to speak, not at all to the wife of their father whom he has put away, but to their mother, who bore them. And let them speak calling her to repentance, so that she may put away her fornications from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts. A fornicatress is one who couples with many. An adulteress is one who, deserting one husband, is joined to another.

She has not preserved the genuineness of love toward me, but rather she denied the intimacy and underestimated the purity of spiritual communion with me. Nor was she willing to bring forth the fruits of my will.

And I will make her like a wilderness, and set her like a pathless land, and kill her with thirst. LXX: And I will make her as a desert, and set her as a land without water, and slay her in thirst. If she will not be converted to better things, I will do to her what I did in the wilderness, so that, led into captivity, they may fall in a foreign land, suffering thirst for all good things, and be unable to return to their homeland. Or at least let them hear in the Gospel: Your house will be left to you desolate. And the Lord will send them not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water; but a famine of hearing the word of the Lord. Of which Isaiah also speaks: They will be like a garden that has no water. The heretics who have been cast off by the Lord, if they do not return to their former home, will suffer such want of all things that even what they seem to have, though false, will be reduced to nothing.

And on her children I will have no mercy, since they are children of fornications, for their mother has played the harlot. She who conceived them is confounded, for she said: I will go after my lovers, who give me bread and my waters, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink. LXX: And on her children I will have no mercy, since they are children of fornication, for their mother has played the harlot. She who bore them is confounded; for she said: I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, and my garments and my linens, and my oil and all things that are necessary to me. This I will do besides to her to whom I said: not my wife, and I am not your husband, and I will make her like a wilderness, and make her like a pathless land. For when I led her out of Egypt, the parents were slain and their sons entered the land of promise. But now the children of the fornicating mother will perish with their harlot mother, since they are children of fornication, and evil ones begotten of evil ones. To them it is said in the Gospel: Brood of vipers, a brood which came to such shamelessness that it heard through Jeremiah: You have got the face of a harlot; you are shameless.

Is not this the mark of a hard brow and of a harlot's shamelessness, to glory in one's own crime and say: I will follow my lovers; I will go to the idols which have supplied me with what is necessary both for food and for clothing? All the things which the prophetic word describes the Jews received spiritually from the Lord. And because they denied the Son of God, choosing for themselves Barabbas, the author of robbery and sedition, and crucifying the Son of God, therefore to this day they follow demons, and ascribe the benefits of God to those who have destroyed the souls of their worshippers. The heretics have bread and waters: their bread is the bread of mourning, and their waters are muddy, waters which choke and kill the baptized. They have also wool from scabby sheep, and flax that remains in its blackness, and oil, of which the prophet says: Let not the oil of the sinner fatten my head, and the drink of the waters of Egypt, of which Jeremiah cries out: What have you to do with the way of Egypt, to drink the water of Gihon? And: What have you to do with the way of the Assyrians, to drink the waters of the rivers? We run through all these things briefly, so as to pass on to the rest.

Who is that adulterous woman whom the prophet Hosea points out, who said, "I will go after my lovers, that give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, and everything that befits me?" Let us grant that we may understand this also of the people of the Jews that went astray; yet whom else are the false Christians (such as are all heretics and schismatics) wont to imitate, except false Israelites?

They, therefore, who are wicked, evildoers, carnal, fleshly, devilish, think that they receive at the hands of their seducers what are the gifts of God alone, whether sacraments, or any spiritual workings about present salvation. But these men have not love towards God, but are busied about those by whose pride they are led astray, and are compared to the adulterous woman, whom the prophet introduces as saying, "I will go after my lovers, that give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, and my oil, and everything that befits me." For thus arise heresies and schisms, when the fleshly people which is not founded on the love of God says, "I will go after my lovers," with whom, either by corruption of her faith, or by the puffing up of her pride, she shamefully commits adultery. But for the sake of those who, having undergone the difficulties, and straits, and barriers of the empty reasoning of those by whom they are led astray, afterwards feel the prickings of fear, and return to the way of peace, to seeking God in all sincerity,—for their sake He goes on to say, "Therefore, behold, I will hedge up thy way with thorns, and make a wall, that she shall not find her paths. And she shall follow after her lovers, but she shall not overtake them: and she shall seek them, but she shall not find them: then shall she say, I will go and return to my first husband; for then was it better with me than now." Then, that they may not attribute to their seducers what they have that is sound, and derived from the doctrine of truth, by which they lead them astray to the falseness of their own dogmas and dissensions; that they may not think that what is sound in them belongs to them, he immediately added, "And she did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oil, and multiplied her money; but she made vessels of gold and silver for Baal."

And hence it comes that for the most part when instead of good things we ask for the opposite, our prayer is either heard but tardily or not at all; and again the Lord vouchsafes to bring upon us even against our will, like some most beneficent physician, for our good what we think is opposed to it, and sometimes He delays and hinders our injurious purposes and deadly attempts from having their horrible effects, and, while we are rushing headlong towards death, draws us back to salvation, and rescues us without our knowing it from the jaws of hell.

And this care of His and providence with regard to us the Divine word has finely described by the prophet Hosea under the figure of Jerusalem as an harlot, and inclining with disgraceful eagerness to the worship of idols, where when she says: "I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread, and my water, and my wool, and my flax, and my oil, and my drink;" the Divine consideration replies having regard to her salvation and not to her wishes: "Behold I will hedge up thy way with thorns, and I will stop it up with a wall, and she shall not find her paths. And she shall follow after her lovers, and shall not overtake them: and she shall seek them, and shall not find them, and shall say: I will return to my first husband, because it was better with me then than now." And again our obstinacy, and scorn, with which we in our rebellious spirit disdain Him when He urges us to a salutary return, is described in the following comparison: He says: "And I said thou shalt call Me Father, and shalt not cease to walk after Me. But as a woman that despiseth her lover, so hath the house of Israel despised Me, saith the Lord." Aptly then, as He has compared Jerusalem to an adulteress forsaking her husband, He compares His own love and persevering goodness to a man who is dying of love for a woman. For the goodness and love of God, which He ever shows to mankind,-since it is overcome by no injuries so as to cease from caring for our salvation, or be driven from His first intention, as if vanquished by our iniquities,-could not be more fitly described by any comparison than the case of a man inflamed with most ardent love for a woman, who is consumed by a more burning passion for her, the more he sees that he is slighted and despised by her.
The Third Conference of Abbot Chaeremon, Chapters 7-8

And also in Hosea, where it is said of Jerusalem committing fornication: Behold, I will close her ways with thorns, and I will block up her paths, and she will not find her track, and she will pursue her lovers, and will not overtake them, and she will seek them, and will not find them; and she will say: I will go and return to my former husband, for it was better with me then than now. Notice that unless the ways had been closed and the paths fenced off, and unless the Lord had destroyed her ways, the fornicating soul could never have said: I will go and return to my former husband.

But if, following the sense above, we wish to take Now the daughter shall be blocked with a blockade as said of the Church, let us bring forward that example from Hosea, in which the adulteress speaks: I will go after my lovers, who gave me my bread, and my water, and my garments, and my linens, my oil, and all things that profit me. And afterwards God, wishing to hinder her most wicked thought, does not let her fulfill what she desires, but blocks her ways, so that she may not overtake her lovers and commit fornication further. For he says: Therefore, behold, I will block her ways with stakes, and I will hedge up her ways, and she will not find her path; and she will pursue her lovers, and will not lay hold of them, and she will seek them, and will not find them, and she will say: I will go and return to my former husband, because it was well with me. Notice that the Lord's work has succeeded: for the adulteress, not finding her way and not able to go where she wished, returns, bound by necessity, to her former husband, and confesses that it is better for her in her former husband's house than it once had been with her lovers; and Israel is schooled by tribulations and blows.

Because of this, behold, I will hedge up your way with thorns, and I will hedge it with a wall, and she will not find her paths, and she will follow her lovers and will not overtake them, and she will seek them and will not find them, and she will say: I will go and return to my first husband, for it was well with me then, more than now. LXX: Therefore, behold, I will hedge up her way with stakes, and I will block her ways; and she will not find her path. And she will pursue her lovers, and will not overtake them; and she will seek them and will not find them; and she will say: I will go and return to my first husband, for it was better with me then than it is now. The harlot had said: I will go after my lovers, who have supplied me with abundance of all things. The Lord answered: I will hedge up your way with thorns, or with stakes, so that you cannot go where you desire, and I will set a hedge-wall, or a wall, in the way, and you will not find your paths which you had often trodden with your foot, so that you may not overtake those whom you were following with such zeal, and, compelled by the need of things, you may return to your husband; and say that saying from the Gospel: How many hired servants in my father's house have bread in abundance, but I perish here with hunger. I will arise and go to my father and will say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you, I am no longer worthy to be called your son, make me as one of your hired servants. From this we understand that by the providence of God evils often befall us, so that we may not have the things we desire, and, oppressed by the various calamities and miseries of this world, we may be compelled to return to the service of God. And by the lovers of Jerusalem and of the Jewish nation, according to the history of that time, let us understand the Assyrians and Chaldeans and Egyptians and the other nations, with whose idols she played the harlot, and from whom, in time of war and when evils pressed upon her, she hoped for help in vain. According to the spiritual understanding, the heretics follow these lovers, and, often deserted by them, return under the weight of their evils to the bosom of mother Church. For through all scourges and torments Israel is instructed.

For hence is that which the Lord says, under the character of every soul, to Judaea who is weak, and walking in evil ways; "Behold, I will hedge up thy way with thorns, and I will hedge it up with a wall, and she shall not find her paths, and she shall follow after her lovers, and she shall not overtake them, and she shall seek them, and not finding them shall say, I will go and return to my first husband, for then it was better with me than now." For the ways of the Elect are hedged up with thorns, when they find the pain of piercing in that which they desire in this world. He obstructs, as it were, by interposing a wall, the ways of those, whose desires the difficulty of attainment opposes. Their souls truly seek their lovers, and find them not, when by following malignant spirits, they do not gain hold of those pleasures of this world, which they desire. But it is well added that she says immediately in consequence of this very difficulty; "I will go and return to my former husband, for then it was better with me than now." For the Lord is the first husband, Who united to Himself the chaste soul, by means of the love of the Holy Spirit. And the mind of each one then longs for Him, when it finds manifold bitternesses, as thorns in those delights, which it desires in this world. For when the mind has begun to be stung by the adversities of the world which it loves, it then understands more fully, how much better it was for it with its former husband. Those then, whom an evil will perverts, adversity frequently corrects.
Morals on the Book of Job, Book 34:3

For there are some who understand the good things they ought to do, but cease from doing them; they see what they ought to do, but do not follow it out of desire. To these, as we said above, it often happens that the adversity of this world strikes them in their carnal desires; they try to grasp temporal glory and cannot; and while they propose to sail through the deep waters, as it were, toward the greater concerns of this age, they are always driven back by contrary winds to the shores of their own dejection. And when they see themselves broken in their desires, with the world opposing them, they are reminded what they owe to their Creator, so that they return to Him with shame, whom they had abandoned in their pride for love of the world.

For often some who wish to advance toward temporal glory either waste away in prolonged illness, or fall crushed by injuries, or are afflicted when struck by heavy losses, and in the sorrow of the world they see that they should have placed no confidence in its pleasures, and reproaching themselves for their own desires, they turn their hearts to God. Of these indeed the Lord says through the prophet: "Behold, I will hedge up your way with thorns, and I will wall it in with a barrier, and she shall not find her paths; and she shall follow after her lovers, and shall not overtake them; she shall seek them, and shall not find them, and she shall say: I will go and return to my first husband, because it was better with me then than now." The husband of every faithful soul is God, because she is joined to Him through faith. But that soul which had been joined to God follows after her lovers, when the mind which has already believed through faith still subjects itself in action to unclean spirits, seeks the glory of the world, feeds on carnal delight, and is nourished by exquisite pleasures. But often almighty God mercifully looks upon such a soul and mingles bitterness with her pleasures. Hence He says: "Behold, I will hedge up your ways with thorns." For our ways are hedged with thorns when in what we wrongly desire we find the pricks of pain. "And I will wall them in with a barrier, and she shall not find her paths." Our ways are walled in with a barrier when hard obstacles in this world resist our desires. And we cannot find our paths, because we are prevented from obtaining what we wrongly seek. "And she shall follow after her lovers, and shall not overtake them; she shall seek them, and shall not find them"; because the soul does not at all attain the fulfillment of her desires from the malign spirits to whom she had subjected herself in her desires. But what great benefit arises from this salutary adversity He adds when it follows: "And she shall say: I will go and return to my first husband, because it was better with me then than now." Therefore, after she finds her ways hedged with thorns, after she cannot overtake her lovers, she returns to the love of her first husband, because often after we cannot obtain what we want in this world, after we grow weary in earthly desires from their impossibility, then we bring God back to mind, then He who displeased us begins to please; and He whose precepts had been bitter to us suddenly becomes sweet in memory; and the sinful soul who had tried to be an adulteress, yet could not through open act, resolves to be a faithful wife. Those therefore who, broken by the adversities of this world, return to the love of God and are corrected from the desires of the present life—what are they, my brothers, but compelled to enter?

Concerning such people the Lord speaks to the prophet under the figure of Jerusalem, saying: Behold, I will hedge your way with thorns, and I will fence it with a wall, and she will not find her paths. And she will follow her lovers and will not overtake them; she will seek them and will not find them (Hosea 2:6). Our lovers are carnal desires; we follow our lovers when we labor in this, that we may become possessors of riches, so that we may have the means to satisfy carnal desires. We follow our lovers and do not overtake them when, with the mercy of God preventing us, we are not able to reach that which we uselessly desire.

So, then, understand that your soul too has had many lovers, who delighted in her beauty, with whom she played the harlot. Concerning whom she also said: "I will go after my lovers, who give me my wine and my oil", and the rest. But now she has come to that time when she says: "I will return to my former husband, because it was better for me then than now". You have returned, then, to your former husband; without doubt you have given offense to your lovers, with whom you were committing adulteries. Unless, therefore, you now abide with your husband in whole faith, and are glued to him with your whole love, out of the many crimes which you have committed every movement of yours and glance of yours is suspect to him, and your very gait, if it be too careless. He can see nothing further in you that is wanton, nothing dissolute and prodigal. But when you turn your eyes even a little away from your husband, at once there must needs come a remembrance of former things. Therefore, that you may both blot out former things and that trust may be able to be had in you for the rest, you must not only do nothing unchaste, but not even think it.

And she did not know this, that I gave her grain and wine and oil, and multiplied silver for her, and gold, which they made into Baal. LXX: And she did not know that I gave her grain and wine and oil, and multiplied silver for her; but these she made into things of silver and gold for Baal. He is answering what came before, for she had said: I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, wool and flax, and my oil and my drink; all of which she had received so that she might turn them to the worship of God. But she, the bread that strengthens and the wine that gladdens the heart of man, and the oil that enlightens every man coming into this world, and the silver of which we have often said: The words of the Lord, chaste words, silver tested by fire, proved for the earth, purified sevenfold; and the gold of which we read: If you sleep in the midst of the lots, the wings of a dove covered with silver, and the hinder parts of her back in the greenness of gold, she turned into idols, and made Baal, which is interpreted 'higher' and 'devouring', while she either thinks that she has greater dogmas than those of the Church, or is devoured in the very knowledge of false opinion. But that, according to the letter, Jerusalem abounded in gold and silver and all riches, and made idols to Baal, the demon of the Sidonians, or, as some more rightly judge, the Babylonian one, from whom he is also called Bel, Ezekiel sets out more fully in his volume, and the whole choir of the prophets relates.

For an unclean spirit dwelt in us before we believed, before we came to Christ, when still, as I said above, our soul was fornicating away from God and was with its lovers, the demons. But after she said: "I will return to my former husband" and came to Christ, who from the beginning "created her according to his own image", the adulterous spirit necessarily gave place when it saw the lawful husband. We have been received, then, by Christ, and our house has been "cleansed" from former sins and "adorned" with the ornaments of the sacraments of the faithful, which those who have been initiated know. But this house does not at once merit to have Christ as its inhabitant, unless its life and conduct be so holy, so pure and undefiled, that it may merit to be a "temple of God". For it must be no longer a house, but a temple, in which God may dwell. If, then, it neglect the grace received and entangle itself in worldly affairs, straightway that unclean spirit returns and claims for itself the empty house.

Therefore I will return and take my grain in its time, and my wine in its time, and I will set free my wool and my flax, which covered her disgrace. LXX: Therefore I will return and take away my wheat in its time, and my wine in its time, and I will take away my garments and my linens, so that they may not cover her disgrace. The punishment is heavier when, at the time of harvest and vintage, the hoped-for crops and the wine are taken away, and are, as it were, snatched out of the hands that already held them. But if at the time of the threshing floor and the vat and the winepress, when the earth makes up for past barrenness with new crops, there is a want of all things, what must we reckon of the rest of the year, when the old stores too are being saved? Now the wool and the flax, or the garments and the linens, are set free, so that they may no longer cover the harlot's disgrace; that is to say, so that she may be stripped of God's help, and the protection of all the angels may depart from her. Hence the Apostle too says that the creation is set free from the bondage of corruption into the liberty of the glory of the sons of God. Many have received the gold and silver of wisdom and eloquence, out of which they might make the lampstand of seven lamps of purest gold, and the golden table of the showbread, and the mercy seat and the cherubim gleaming with the splendor of gold, and the silver bases of the pillars, and the wheat of the word of God, and the wine, the joy of the Holy Spirit; and garments too and linens with which believers might be clothed in Christ; all of which they turned to the worship of idolatry, composing various dogmas of error, and, being deceived, they deceived others. All these things God takes away, so that those who did not perceive the giver from abundance may perceive him from want.

These things, both according to the history and according to tropology, unhappy Judea has suffered: all her shame has been uncovered in the eyes of the Gentiles, and no one could rescue her from the hands of God. All the ceremonies have ceased, the festivity has been turned into mourning; all that she thought was given her by the demons, she now knows has been taken away because she offended God. First the Assyrians and the Chaldeans devoured her, the Medes and the Persians and the Macedonians; at the last the most savage beast tore her apart, the empire of the Romans, whose name is passed over in silence in Daniel, so that the dread of those who are to be devoured may be made greater. What we have said of Judea, refer to the heretics, who, promising doctrine and knowledge at first sight, having gone out from the Church, are deserted by God; and all their disgrace is set in the sight of their lovers, whom they had deceived before; and, handed over to the beasts which the prophet shuns when he says, Do not hand over to the beasts the soul that confesses you, they will be left to their bites.

So then, once the garment and the linen have been set free, so that they might no longer cover the disgrace of the fornicating woman, all the shame of Jerusalem, or the folly through which she worked shame, will be uncovered in the sight of her lovers, so that those who desired her veiled may despise her exposed. And when she has been handed over to her lovers the Assyrians, or to the demons whom both she herself and the Assyrians serve, no one, he says, will be able to snatch her from my hand; for the weakness of the demons is proved in this, that those whom they had received abounding in all things they cannot free when they are crushed by evils.

And handed over to Babylonian slavery, she will by no means be able to celebrate the three solemnities of Passover and Pentecost and Tabernacles, nor to keep the joy of the new moon, that is, of the calends, nor of the sabbath, nor all the festivals, which he comprises under one name.

And now I will uncover her folly in the eyes of her lovers; and no one will rescue her from my hand and I will make all her joy cease, her solemnity, her new moon, her sabbath, and all her festal times; and I will spoil her vine and her fig tree, of which she said: These are my wages, which my lovers gave me; and I will make her into a forest, and the beast of the field will eat her. LXX: And now I will uncover her uncleanness in the sight of her lovers; and no one will rescue her from my hand; and I will turn away all her gladness, her solemnities and her new moons, and the sabbaths, and all her festivals; and I will destroy her vine, and her fig trees, of which she said: These are my wages which my lovers gave me; and I will make her a testimony, and the beasts of the field will eat her. What follows, The birds of the sky and the creeping things of the earth, must be marked beforehand with an obelus. For 'forest', too, which in Hebrew is called iar, whence Kiriath-jearim also is interpreted 'town of the woods', the LXX translated 'testimony', through the deceptive likeness of the letters res and daleth. For if daleth is read in place of res, it means 'testimony', provided only that the letter iod does not come before it.

The vine too and the fig tree and the abundance of all things will be spoiled: in the vine understand gladness, in the fig sweetness and pleasantness, which are taken away by the evils of a most grievous slavery; and they are taken away for this reason, that she judged them given to her not by God, as to a wife, but by her lovers, as to a harlot, for the wages of lust. Then she will by no means have fruit-bearing trees, but everything will be turned into forest. And since he had once taken the metaphor from the woods, he carries it through in the rest, so as to call the enemies, by whom all things are to be devoured, beasts.

And I will visit upon her the days of the Baalim, on which she burned incense and adorned herself with her earring and her necklace, and went after her lovers, and forgot me, says the Lord. LXX: And I will avenge upon her the days of the Baalim, on which she sacrificed to them; and she put her earrings and necklaces about herself, and went after her lovers; but me she forgot, says the Lord. He keeps up the character of the harlot, who adorns herself with gold and gems to please her lovers, and whatever beauty she does not have by nature she procures by art. These earrings, with which her ears had been adorned by the teaching of God, and these pearls which hung precious from her neck, so that the bridegroom and husband said to her, Your neck is like necklaces, she cast before the feet of swine, and gave what is holy to the dogs. And what we read in Proverbs was fulfilled: Like a golden earring in a sow's nostrils, so is beauty to a most wicked woman. Now she did all these things so as to follow her lovers and leave her husband. And so great was her desire for pleasure and lust that she lost all memory of her marriage and forgot that she had been a wife. Therefore, on those very solemnities on which she burned frankincense to the demons, she will be visited with blows and chastised with punishments. Baal in the singular number, Baalim in the plural: the same idols are named in the masculine gender. For wherever we read the syllable im at the end of a Hebrew word, it is in the plural number, masculine gender; but where oth, plural number, feminine gender.
