Therefore we understand seraphim and cherubim as plural number, masculine gender; but Sabaoth, which is interpreted 'of armies', or 'of hosts', or 'of powers', as plural number, feminine gender. And so the Baalim too are of the masculine gender and plural number, although some wrongly read τῇ Βαὰλ (feminine article) and ταῖς Βααλεὶμ (feminine plural), in the feminine gender. But how the heretics deceive their lovers, and adorn themselves with charm of speech and the arrangement of words, so as to make falsehood look like truth, and abandon conjugal chastity, and burn incense to the Baalim, that is, to the idols which they have fashioned out of their own heart, we see daily. For they have no care for the simple rusticity that does not seek a harlot's ornaments, but for artful and elegant falsehood, so as to please their lovers, the devils and demons.

For this reason God says of Jerusalem too: Behold, I will lead her astray, and I will make her like a desert, and set her like a land without water, and I will speak to her heart; and I will give her possessions from there, and the valley of Achor to open understanding (Hos 2:14, 15). Let us consider the order of each thing: he leads her astray, and makes her deserted and without water, so that she may suffer thirst for the virtues. After she has said, My soul has thirsted for you, how many ways my flesh for you (Ps 62 [63]:2), then he will speak to her heart and console her as she mourns. And he will give her a possession from there, that is, from the repentance and sorrow which works salvation. And the humility of her troubled heart (for this is what the valley of Achor means) opens her understanding, so that she may not be ignorant of her Creator.

Therefore, behold, I will allure her; and I will lead her into the wilderness, and I will speak to her heart. And I will give her her vinedressers from the same place, and the valley of Achor to open up hope. LXX: Therefore, behold, I will lead her astray and will make her like a desert; and I will speak to her heart and give her her possessions from there, and the valley of Achor to open up her understanding. Where we said to open up hope, and the LXX rendered to open up her understanding, Symmachus interpreted εἰς θύραν ἐλπίδος, that is, into a door of hope, Theodotion διανοῖξαι τὴν ὑπομονὴν αὐτῆς, that is, to open up her patience, or her expectation. After the disgrace of Jerusalem, or of Judea the harlot, has been uncovered in the eyes of her lovers, and every solemnity has ceased, and drought or hail has spoiled the vineyard and the fig tree, and, reduced to woods and fruitless trees, she has been devoured by beasts, and the Lord has repaid her with tortures and torments, because she had burned frankincense to the demons, the Baalim, and she thinks that she can by no means rise again any more from the ashes and embers, then, that is, at the coming of Christ his Son, he will open the hope of salvation, and give room for repentance, and will caress her; for this is what I will allure her means; so as to soften her former pains, after the greatness of her punishments, by the promise of prosperity. And I will lead her, he says, into the wilderness, that is, I will lead her out of evils, just as I had earlier led her out of Egyptian slavery; and I will speak to her heart soft words, words of comfort, so as to temper sadness with joy, according to the idiom of the Scriptures, in which words Shechem too spoke to the heart of Dinah, and Joseph in Egypt to his brothers, who were sad and afraid, so that grief might be changed into joy.

These things the circumcision and our own Judaizers refer to the reign of a thousand years, things which we see fulfilled in the beginning through the apostles as vinedressers and the many thousands of believers from Israel, and being fulfilled daily in those who are willing to believe. And where we said, I will allure her, and the LXX interpreted, I will lead her astray, they refer it to the time of the Antichrist, so that those who did not receive the truth of Christ may receive that one's lie, and afterwards, when Christ comes, may be saved.

"Behold, I will mislead her" not from what is necessary and useful to life … but from the things that are shameful and harmful to the fulfillment of any enjoyment.… And as her ways are usefully hedged around with thorns so that she may not lay hold of her lovers, in the same manner she believes herself—now running downhill toward ruin and destruction—to be led astray by the mercy of God when she is brought to desire virtue. Having received the light of the knowledge of God in mind and heart, as I said, she is no longer able to find her old path.

Since she [Israel] is accessible like a well-watered land to the herds of demons, he [the Lord] promises to treat her as a wilderness.… He will display it to their desires as an austere, untrodden and waterless place, so that finding no resting place they will despise it and depart.

We who have Christ, the author of necessary things dwelling inside the heart, were at once enriched in every kind of virtue, and in the abundant and inalienable possession of the spiritual gifts.… He promises to speak in her heart. For the synagogue of the Judeans, exactly as the church from the nations, will be called to awareness by taking into mind the divine laws inscribed through the Spirit.
Speaking directly to the heart indicates the promulgation of the law, which shaped the hearts of the listener.

And what follows: And I will give her her vinedressers from the same place. He who had set forth beforehand the caressing and the wilderness in the likeness of the past history of those who went out of Egypt, in which Moses and Aaron arose as princes from the same nation of the Jews, now too promises that he will give her vinedressers from the same place. That the vineyard is understood as Israel, all the scripture of both the Old and the New Testament bears witness: The vineyard of the Lord of Sabaoth is the house of Israel. And: You transferred a vineyard out of Egypt. And in the Gospel: The householder let out his vineyard and did not receive the fruits. And when his son had been killed, at the last he let it out to other vinedressers. This, then, is what the prophetic word promises: that the princes of this vineyard, going out from the nations and from the captivity of enemies, or of vices, should be of the very race of the Jews, that is, the apostles; and that the place of tumult and valley of troubles — for this is what Achor is interpreted — should be changed into a door of hope, or to open up hope and patience, in that she has suffered punishments and torments for this reason, that through them she might come to prosperity. But that the valley of Achor, in which Achan was killed for the theft of the things that had been consecrated to God, is interpreted 'confusion' and 'tumult', and not, as some think, διαστροφὴ, that is, perversity, Joshua himself interprets when he speaks to Achan: Because you have troubled us, may the Lord trouble you on this day. Hence that place was called Emec Achor, that is, the valley of confusion. And at the same time we understand this too: that at the beginning of the holy land, near Jericho, when the people came out of the wilderness, beside the streams of the Jordan, in Israel's first victory, grief was changed into joy, and hope was opened there, where there had been despair. So that, once those have been punished who sinned against Christ and committed sacrilege, those of them may be saved who have detested the blaspheming Jews and, as far as was in their power, have slain them.

And she will sing there according to the days of her youth, and according to the days of her coming up from the land of Egypt. LXX: And she will be humbled according to the days of her infancy and according to the days of the coming up from the land of Egypt. In the place where we put she will sing, and the LXX translated she will be humbled, in the Hebrew is written anatha, which Symmachus interpreted 'she will be afflicted', Theodotion 'she will answer', Aquila 'she will obey', that is, ὑπακούσει; we take it rather from the Hebrew κατὰ λέξιν (word for word), that is, 'she will lead the singing'; so that, since he had once set down the being tossed about and the leading out into the wilderness, and the vinedressers from the same place, and the valley of Achor, touching in brief speech on the whole history of those who went out of Egypt and journeyed to the holy land, he might even now keep the likeness of the history. So that, just as at that time, when they were going out of the land of Egypt, after Pharaoh had been drowned in the Red Sea, Miriam took up a timbrel and, leading the singing for the others, exulted and said: Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously magnified; horse and rider he has cast into the sea, so now too, according to the days of her youth, or of her adolescence, when she went out of the land of Egypt, she may sing and rejoice, and sing together of the kingdom of Christ and her own salvation among the choirs of the Church. And notice that when we go out of Egypt and pass over to better things, we are said to go up, because Jerusalem is set in the mountains; and he who had wished to go down from it into Jericho was wounded. But to those who seek the help of Egypt, that is, of this world, it is said: Woe to those who go down into Egypt for help. The interpretation of Aquila and Theodotion, of whom the one put ὑπακούσει, that is, 'will hear', the other ἀποκριθήσεται, that is, 'will answer', is on our side, in that while some lead the singing, others answer, singing together. But she will be humbled and she will be afflicted, which the LXX and Symmachus translated, does not suit a time of gladness, unless perhaps she will imitate Paul, who, after he was called as an apostle, bewails his former sins and says that he is unworthy of the calling of an apostle, because he persecuted the Church of God; so that the humiliation and the affliction are to be taken as the awareness of a past wound, not as pain at present evils.

Whatever is necessary for life and understanding of God's knowledge in Christ, through whom and in whom we saw the Father, enriched in unfading hope—as I said, in glory, pride of adoption, of grace and of reigning together with Christ himself—these are the possessions of the saints; this is the heavenly wealth.

[Israel] will be humble and obedient just as in the beginning, when she was born to the knowledge of God through the law and gladly received the decree of the divine adoption. Accordingly, he calls the regeneration to the knowledge of God through the law the "days [of her youth]."

Just as those at that early time have learned through Achan's punishment how serious is the transgression of the law, in the same manner these will come to the realization of their own trespasses through the captivity.

And it will be on that day, says the Lord, she will call me My husband, and will no longer call me Baalim; and I will take away the names of the Baalim from her mouth, and she will no longer remember their name. LXX: likewise. That Ninus, the son of Belus, was the first to reign over all Asia, all histories, both Greek and barbarian, relate; he founded among the Assyrians the city of Ninus, named after himself, which the Hebrews call Nineveh. His wife Semiramis, of whom many marvelous things are told, built the walls of Babylon. Of her the famous poet bears witness, saying: "Where Semiramis is said once to have girded the city with walls of baked brick." He fought in a strong contest against the great Zoroaster, king of the Bactrians, and came to such glory that he enrolled his father Belus as a god; he is called Bel in Hebrew, and in many prophets, and above all in Daniel according to Theodotion, he is called by this name as the idol of Babylon. The Sidonians and Phoenicians call him Baal; for between the consonant letters beth and lamed the same vowel letter ain is placed, which, according to the peculiar character of that language, is read now Beel, now Baal. Hence Dido too, the Sidonian of royal race, when she had received Aeneas as a guest, pours a libation of wine to Jupiter from that bowl which Belus and all those descended from Belus were accustomed to use. We have learned the origin of the demon, or rather of a man consecrated into a demon; for all idols have grown out of the error concerning the dead. Let us hear the rest: in the Hebrew and Syrian tongue Baal is interpreted ἔχων, that is, 'having'. If we wish to say 'having me', let us say Baali; and among both nations wives call their husbands Baali, that is, 'my husband', which is understood as 'having me'; and the sense is: he who has me in marriage. In the same language of the Hebrews a man is called is, whence the wife too, who was taken from the man, is called Issa in Genesis, as virago, as it were, from vir, man.

What God says, then, is this: since with both words, that is, Issi and Baali, 'my husband', or 'my spouse', is named, I so hate the names of idols that even what can rightly be said I would by no means wish to be said, because of the ambiguity and the likeness of the word, but wish to be called Issi rather than Baali, lest while she says one thing she should remember another, and, naming her husband, think of an idol. Forgive the obscurity, which arises in three ways: either from the difficulty of the matters, or from the inexperience of the teacher, or from the excessive slowness of the learner. For in expounding a Hebrew prophet I ought not to play with little oratorical declamations, and to sing in narrations and epilogues in the Asiatic manner, but, with the help of your prayers and with an incredible zeal for learning, to open what is closed. Finally Aquila, a diligent and painstaking translator: She will call, he says, me My husband, and will no longer call me Having me, that is, Baal.

For He hath come as a Physician, not as a Judge. Therefore in like manner as those of old took harlots for wives, even so God too espoused unto Himself the nature which had played the harlot: and this also prophets from the beginning declare to have taken place with respect to the Synagogue. But that spouse was ungrateful towards Him who had been an husband to her, whereas, the Church, when once delivered from the evils received from our fathers, continued to embrace the Bridegroom.
HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 3:5

And I will strike a covenant for them in that day with the beast of the field, and with the bird of the sky, and with the creeping thing of the earth; and the bow, and the sword, and war I will crush out of the land; and I will make them sleep confidently. LXX: And I will arrange a covenant for them in that day with the beasts of the field, and with the flying things of the sky, and with the creeping things of the earth; and the bow, and the sword, and war I will crush out of the land; and I will make them dwell in hope. When all the names of the hostile religion have been taken away from the people that confesses the Lord, and she calls me, he says, My husband, and by no means Baali, that is, my idol, then I will strike a covenant and concord for them with the beasts of the field, and the birds of the sky, and the creeping things of the earth. Of this time Isaiah also speaks: The wolf will dwell with the lamb; and the leopard will lie down with the kid. The calf, and the lion, and the sheep will abide together, and a little child will drive them. The calf and the bear will feed, and their young will rest together; and the lion will eat straw like the ox, by no means desiring flesh and blood, but feeding on clean and simple foods. When it was revealed to Peter, that he might receive Cornelius from the nations, and he was commanded to eat all the beasts and to know that nothing is unclean which is received with thanksgiving, concerning which he afterwards hears: What God has cleansed, do not call common. Therefore at the coming of the Lord the Savior, after the triumphs of his resurrection and his ascent to the Father, the two walls were joined by the cornerstone, by him who made both one. And he called her who was called Without Mercy, Obtained Mercy; and him who was called Not My People, his own people; and when all things have been made peaceful, the bow and the sword will be crushed, and war. For the instruments of fighters will not be necessary when those who would fight are lacking. Israel will be joined to the nations, and that saying of Deuteronomy will be fulfilled: Rejoice, you nations, with his people. Known for in Judea is God, in Israel his name is great. And: His place has been made in peace, and his dwelling in Zion, that is, in the Church, in which he broke the powers, the bow, the shield, the sword and war; and when these have been broken and crushed, the believers will sleep confidently and will rest under one shepherd. Or: they will hope in those things which eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and which have not entered into the heart of man, which God has prepared for those who love him.

Who would not grieve over such things and say, “How is the faithful city become an harlot?” How would not the Lord Himself say to some of those who are now walking in the spirit of Jeremiah, “Hast thou seen what the virgin of Israel has done to me?” I betrothed her to me in trust, in purity, in righteousness, in judgment, in pity, and in mercy; as I promised her through Hosea the prophet. But she loved strangers, and while I, her husband, was yet alive, she is called adulteress, and is not afraid to belong to another husband.

You have wisely thought it a subject of inquiry, whether there be any difference in God's love towards those who have believed from their childhood, and those who have believed in the course of their youth or more advanced age; for this also has not been past over nor left unnoticed in the sacred Scriptures. For it is not without meaning that the Lord our God says to the Prophet Joel, Lament to me for the spouse girded with sackcloth and for the husband of her youth, expressing his grief for the Synagogue, who, before, in her virginity, had been espoused to the Word of God, or, it may be, for a soul which had fallen from her good deeds, that by the heinousness of her sins she had incurred hatred, and through the defilement of impiety and the stains of unbelief had become miserable and despised, and far removed from the grace of that Spouse which had before been counted worthy to be told, I will betroth thee unto Me in righteousness and in judgment and in loving kindness and in mercies.

And I will betroth you to me for ever; and I will betroth you to me in justice and judgment, and in mercy and in compassions; and I will betroth you to me in faith, and you will know that I am the Lord. LXX: likewise. O how great is the clemency of God! The harlot who has played the harlot with many lovers, and for her crime was handed over to the beasts, after she returns to her husband, is by no means said to be reconciled to him, but to be betrothed. And see what difference there is between the union of God and that of men: a man, when he has taken a wife, makes a woman out of a virgin, that is, not a virgin; God, even when joined to harlots, changes them into virgins, according to that which is said to the adulteress through Jeremiah: You have not called upon me as lord, or father, or prince of your virginity. Hence the Apostle too speaks to the Corinthians who believed after fornication and the worship of idols: For I have betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. We ask why he repeated the word betrothal a third time. For first he says: I will betroth you to me for ever. Second: I will betroth you to me in justice and judgment, and in mercy and in compassions. And not content with this end, he adds a third as well: I will betroth you to me in faith, and you will know that I am the Lord. First he betrothed her in Abraham, or in Egypt, so that he might have an everlasting wife. Second on Mount Sinai, giving her in the betrothal gifts the justice and judgment of the law, and mercy joined to the law, so that when she sinned she would be handed over to captivity, and when she repented she would be called back to her homeland and obtain mercy. Of these betrothal gifts the psalmist sings in various places: Mercy and judgment I will sing to you, O Lord. And: Mercy and truth have met each other, and justice and peace have kissed each other. These two cups we read of in the seventy-fourth (75th) psalm: A cup in the hand of the Lord, full of unmixed wine, mixed, and he has tilted it from this into that; from the cup of justice into the cup of mercy, and again from the cup of mercy into the cup of justice. If you mark iniquities, he says, O Lord, Lord, who will endure? For with you there is propitiation. This harlot, then, who first had been joined by the vow of the bridegroom in everlasting embraces, so that she should never withdraw from the marriage bond, because she withdrew and played the harlot in Egypt, is taken again through the lawful rites; and because she transgressed this, and the prophets, the friends, as it were, of the bridegroom, who had been sent to her, were killed, last of all came the Son of God, the Lord Jesus; and when he had been crucified and had risen from the dead, she is betrothed by no means in the justice of the law, but in faith and the grace of the Gospel, so that when she has known the Only-begotten, she may know the Father also. For he himself says to Philip: Have I been with you so long a time, and you have not known me? Philip, he who has seen me has seen my Father also; how do you say: Show us the Father? Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father is in me? Whoever has been betrothed in faith and has believed the Gospel will at once know that he himself is God, believing in him whom he had formerly denied.

The sixth degree of chastity is that he not be deluded by the alluring images of women even when asleep. For although we do not believe that this delusion is sinful, nonetheless it is an indication of a desire that is still deeply ingrained. It is evident that this delusion can occur in a number of ways. For each person is tempted, even while asleep, according to how he behaves and thinks while awake. Those who have known sexual intercourse are led astray in one way, those who have had no part in union with a woman in another way. The latter are usually disturbed by simpler and purer dreams, such that they can be cleansed more easily and with less effort. But the former are deceived by filthier and more explicit images until, gradually and according to the measure of chastity for which each is struggling, even the mind that has fallen asleep learns to hate what it used to find pleasurable, and, through the prophet, the Lord grants it what is promised to brave men as the highest reward for their labors: "I will destroy the bow and the sword and war from your land, and I will make you sleep securely."

A betrothed woman was chosen, so that Christ's church might already be symbolically indicated as bride, according to the words of the prophet Hosea: "I will make you my bride in justice and right; I will make you my bride in mercy and benevolence, and I will espouse you in fidelity." Thus John says, "He who has a bride is the bridegroom." And blessed Paul: "I have promised you to one bridegroom, to present you to Christ as a chaste virgin." She is truly a bride who regenerates the new infancy of Christ by a virginal birth.

And it will be in that day: I will hear, says the Lord, I will hear the heavens, and they will hear the earth, and the earth will hear the wheat and the wine and the oil, and these will hear Jezreel, and I will sow her for myself in the land, and I will have mercy on her who was Without Mercy; and I will say to Not My People: You are My People; and he will say: You are my God. LXX: And it will be in that day, says the Lord: I will hear the heaven, and the heaven will hear the earth, and the earth will hear the grain, the wine, and the oil, and these will hear Jezreel, and I will sow her for myself upon the land, and I will love her who was not loved; and I will say to Not My People: You are My People; and he will say: You are the Lord my God. In that day and at that time, when I have betrothed you to me in faith, and you have known that I am the Lord, I will hear the heavens, which tell the glory of God, and the heavens will hear the earth, so as to water it with heavenly rain; and the earth, from which truth has sprung, and into whose field the householder goes out to sow his seed, will hear the wheat and the wine and the oil, of which we spoke above; and all these will hear Jezreel, that is, the seed of God, so that it may be understood that the abundance and fertility of all things are granted on account of the seed of God, who is Christ, because the seed of God is sown in the earth, to bring forth manifold fruits, a hundredfold, sixtyfold and thirtyfold.

Concerning the hearing of heaven and earth, and of the grain, wine and oil, and of Jezreel, some hold this view: that after Christ has come, all things will run in their own order, and the whole creation will serve the advantage of men, as it was founded in the beginning. All these things the Jews and our Judaizers await bodily, after the Antichrist, at the end of the world.

Thou wilt say then unto me, Why doth he yet find fault? For who hath resisted his will?  Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?  Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?  What if God, willing to show his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction:  And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory,  Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?  As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved.  And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God. [Hosea 2:23] Esaias also crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved:  For he will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness: because a short work will the Lord make upon the earth.  And as Esaias said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and been made like unto Gomorrha.

Next the promise of God is said for those who hear; if they do what is "commanded: And you will be my people and I will be your God." Not everyone who says they are a people of God are "a people" of God. Hence, that people who were proclaimed to be a people of God heard, "You are not my people," in the passage, "Therefore you are not my people." And it has been said to that people you are "not my people." Elsewhere this people was called a "people," for "they have provoked me to jealousy with what is not God"—he speaks concerning the former—"they have provoked me with their idols. So I will provoke them to jealousy with those who are not a people, with a senseless nation I will provoke them."

And not only is the operation of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit everywhere one but also there is one and the same will, calling, and giving of commands, which one may see in the great and saving mystery of the Church. For as the Father called the Gentiles to the Church, saying: "I will call her My people which was not My people, and her beloved who was not beloved;" and elsewhere: "My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations," so, too, the Lord Jesus said that Paul was chosen by Him to call forth and gather together the Church, as you find it said by the Lord Jesus to Ananias: "Go, for he is a chosen vessel unto Me to bear My name before all nations." As, then, God the Father called the Church, so, too, Christ called it, and so, too, the Spirit called it, saying: "Separate Me Paul and Barnabas for the work to which I have called them." "So," it is added, "having fasted and prayed, they laid hands on them and sent them forth. And they, being sent forth by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia." So Paul received the apostleship by the will not only of Christ, but also of the Holy Spirit, and hastened to gather together the Gentiles.

Having then given to the question that answer which was furnished by facts, in order to give his discourse the advantage of other testimony in its favor, he introduces the prophets also making the same declarations aforetime. For Hosea, he says, of old put this in writing, as follows: "I will call them My people, which were not My people; and her beloved, which was not beloved." Here to prevent their saying, that you are deceiving us here with specious reasoning, he calls Hosea to witness, who crieth and saith, "I will call them My people, who were not My people." Who then are the not-people? Plainly, the Gentiles. And who the not-beloved? The same again. However, he says, that they shall become at once people, and beloved, and sons of God. "For even they shall be called," he says, "the children of the living God." But if they should assert that this was said of those of the Jews who believed, even then the argument stands. For if with those who after so many benefits were hard-hearted and estranged, and had lost their being as a people, so great a change was wrought, what is there to prevent even those who were not estranged after being taken to Him, but were originally aliens, from being called, and, provided they obey, from being counted worthy of the same blessings? Having then done with Hosea, he does not content himself with him only, but also brings Isaiah in after him, sounding in harmony with him.

And that harlot who had been joined to God, and had borne three children, two males and one female, the first Jezreel, the second Without Mercy, the third Not My People, may see that because of the seed of God the names of things have been changed, and that in the faith of Christ she who was Without Mercy has obtained mercy, and he who was formerly called Not a People has been called the people of God. From this we perceive that everything that has been said can be referred both to the ten tribes, which are called Israel, and which under the name of the harlot bore three children, and to the whole race of the Jewish name.

"You who were once not a people but now are the people of God, who did not seek after mercy but now have received mercy." By these verses he indicates clearly that he has written this letter to those who had come from the Gentiles to the faith, who were once separated from the way of life of the people of God but then through the grace of faith were joined to his people and obtained the mercy that they did not know how to hope for. He takes them, however, from the prophet Hosea, who predicted the calling of the Gentiles and said, "I shall call [those who were] not my people my people and [those who did] not receive mercy [a people] having received mercy. And it will be in the place where it was said, 'You are not my people,' there they will be called sons of the living God."
Commentary on the Catholic Epistles, 1 Peter 2:10
3: And the Lord said to me: Go again, love a woman loved by a friend and an adulteress, as the Lord loves the sons of Israel; and they look to other gods, and love the husks of grapes. LXX: And the Lord said to me: Go again and love a woman who loves evil things and an adulteress, as the Lord loves the sons of Israel; and they look to other gods, and love cooked cakes with grape-husks. To the former woman the prophet is joined as a type of the ten tribes, or of the whole Jewish people playing the harlot, and at length he received back into salvation the children who had been cast off and tormented; here he is ordered to love an adulterous woman again. When it is said: again, does it show that he had loved a fornicatress before, who as an adulteress either loves those evil things or is loved by a friend and neighbor? For the Hebrew word Re is read either as evil or as friend. And lest we should think that the prophet's love for the adulteress signifies anything other than God's love for the sons of Israel, he added: as the Lord loves the sons of Israel. Therefore the fact that the prophet loves the adulteress, and yet is not joined to her in marriage nor united with her in fornication, but only loves the woman who does wrong, is a type of God, who loves the most wicked sons of Israel; and they, though they are loved by the Lord, look to other gods and idols, and love the husks of grapes, which have no wine; and they have lost their former grace, like the demons, who, having fallen from their own dignity and possessing nothing of their ancient grace, are dry and withering in an old dryness. Hence for husks, which in Hebrew is called asise, Aquila translated παλαιὰ, that is, old things; Symmachus ἀκάρπους, that is, barren; and they are not only husks, but old husks, so that they bear witness to ancient offenses. And it is to be noted that this adulteress signifies the present time of the Jews, who, without God and the knowledge of the Scriptures and the grace of the Holy Spirit, are loved by the Lord, who awaits the salvation of all and opens the door to those who repent; and nevertheless they love useless things, loving the traditions of men and the dreams of the δευτερωσέων (of the 'secondary teachings', the Jewish traditions), and by no means have grapes and wine and winepresses full of must, but old husks which have been thrown away. For the pemmata, which the LXX translated, and which are eaten with raisins or grape-husks, we can say in Latin flat-cakes, or pastries, which are offered to idols and are called in Greek πόπανα (cakes). But the sons of Israel in the present passage are called the twelve tribes; above, however, the ten which were in Samaria and possessed the metropolis, Jezreel.

These then are that seven and eight whereof Hosea says that by that number he purchased to himself, and acquired the fulness of faith, for thus it is written, So I bought her to me for fifteen pieces of silver, and for an homer of barley, and an half homer of barley, and a measure of wine. But in the former verses God had commanded him to hire to himself an harlot, and it is manifest that he did so, in that he has mentioned the price of her hiring. Now the fifteen pieces of silver are made up of the numbers seven and eight, wherefore they represent these numbers.

And I dug her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver, and a cor of barley, and half a cor of barley, and I said to her: Many days you will wait for me; you will not play the harlot, and you will not be for a man; but I also will wait for you. LXX: And I hired her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver, and a gomor of barley, and a nebel of wine, and I said to her: Many days you will sit for me; and you will not play the harlot, nor will you be for another man, and I for you. For gomor, in the Hebrew is written omer, which all the translators, except the LXX, have rendered cor, a word Greek and especially Palestinian, which holds thirty modii. And for nebel of wine, in the Hebrew is read lethech seorim, which the other translators rendered ἡμίκορον of barley, that is, half a cor, which makes fifteen modii. And what is added in the common edition: Nor will you be for another man; another is not found in the Hebrew, but simply you will not be for a man. For if another is put, it is understood that she is had by her own husband. But when it is said absolutely you will not be for a man, we understand that she is joined to no one at all, and is without marital intercourse. Now the measure of the cor we read in Ezekiel, and in the Gospel. So he dug her for himself, that is, the adulteress, or hired her for fifteen pieces of silver. When he says: I dug, he points to the vineyard which was planted by the Lord and is set down in many places of the Scriptures, signifying the people of the Jews. But if we read: I hired, it is the price of an adulteress, not so that she may sleep with the prophet, but so that, content with her wage, she may cease committing adultery and not be joined here and there to others. She is also dug, or hired, for a cor of barley and half a cor of barley, that is, for forty-five modii; and having received this wage, she heard from the Lord: Many days you will wait for me, or you will sit for me; you will not play the harlot nor be for a man. That is: neither will you shamefully prostitute yourself to other lovers, nor will you be lawfully joined to me, the man by whom you were hired. And lest you think a wrong has been done to you because I said: you will wait for me, I will repay like for like: and I also will wait for you. As the fifteenth day of the month Nisan was dawning, the firstborn of the Egyptians were struck, and the people of Israel was led out of Egypt and hired for a wage into the service of God. Finally, for the firstborn of Israel, which did not feel the common plague, take five shekels of silver each, which are contributed to the gifts of the temple. Most of our writers refer the fifteen to the hebdomad of the law and the ogdoad of the Gospel, that is, the Sabbath and the day of the resurrection, on which spiritual circumcision is practiced. But how an adulterous woman who is fed on barley and is estranged from her husband should receive both testaments as her wage, they cannot explain. On the forty-fifth day the people came to Mount Sinai, and at once on the next day they were commanded to sanctify themselves from intercourse with women for three days, and to prepare themselves to receive the law of God. When the three days had passed, on the fiftieth day Moses went up the mountain and received the Decalogue. So the people of the Jews, which was once hired for fifteen pieces of silver and forty-five modii of barley, has sat since the coming of the Lord the Savior, and awaits the coming of its husband. And when he says: You will not play the harlot, and you will not be for a man, he shows this: that in the meantime she does not now serve idols, and yet does not have God, but has been stripped both of her lovers and of her husband. And because she has no husband, she does not eat the food of men, grain and pulse, but the barley of irrational beasts of burden, chewing over the cheapness of the letter which kills, and not having the spirit which gives life. Hence also in the law, the woman who is accused of adultery by her husband, in the drink of ἐλεγμοῦ, that is, of conviction, when she is proved guilty of sin, receives barley meal; for she who has imitated horses and mules, which have no understanding, is sustained on the food of horses and mules. For half a cor of barley the Seventy translated a nebel of wine, which is not found in the Hebrew at all. And we can say: that in the nebel of wine, that is, a full and finished measure, the adulteress was made drunk and afflicted with full punishments. Hence Jeremiah too gives the cup of unmixed wine to drink to the nations and to Jerusalem. The husband also sits, or rather waits for the repentance of the adulteress, so that after the fullness of the Gentiles has come in, and Israel has believed last, so that what had been the head is turned into the tail, and the tail is turned into the head, then there may be one flock and one shepherd.

And how shall I speak of the whore married by the prophet? She is the figure either of the church as gathered in from the Gentiles, or—an interpretation that better suits the passage—of the synagogue. She, Israel, was first adopted from among the idolaters by Abraham and Moses. She has now denied the Savior and proved unfaithful to him. Therefore she has long been deprived of her altar, priests and prophets and has to abide many days to return to her first husband. For when the faithfulness of the Gentiles shall be fulfilled, all Israel shall be saved.

I ask therefore on what day the manna began to be given from heaven, and I wish to compare our Lord's day with the sabbath of the Jews. For from the divine scriptures it appears that the manna was first given upon the earth on the Lord's day. For if, as Scripture says, it was gathered for six continuous days, but on the seventh day, which is the sabbath, there was a cessation, without doubt its beginning was from the first day, which is the Lord's day. But if from the divine scriptures this is established, that on the Lord's day God rained the manna and on the sabbath he did not rain it, let the Jews understand that even then our Lord's day was preferred to the Jewish sabbath, that even then it was indicated that on their sabbath no grace of God came down to them from heaven, that no heavenly bread, which is the word of God, came to them. For the prophet says also elsewhere: "for many days the children of Israel shall sit without king, without prince, without prophet, without victim, without sacrifice, without priest". But on our Lord's day the Lord always rains manna from heaven.

For the prophecy was fulfilled that had declared, "For the children of Israel shall abide many days without king and prince. There shall be no victim, nor altar, nor priesthood, nor answers." These testimonies, accordingly, we employ against those who presume to assert that what is spoken in Genesis by Jacob refers to Judah. They say that there still remains a prince of the race of Judah—he, namely, who is the prince of their nation, whom they style patriarch—and that there cannot fail [a ruler] of his seed, who will remain until the advent of that Christ whom they picture themselves. But if the prophet's words are true when he says, "The children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, without prince; and there shall be no victim, nor altar, nor priesthood," and if, certainly, since the overthrow of the temple, victims are neither offered, nor any altar found, nor any priesthood exists. So it is most certain that, as it is written, princes have departed from Judah and a leader from between his thighs, until the coming of him for whom it has been reserved. It is established, then, that he has indeed come from whom it has been reserved and in whom is the expectation of the Gentiles. And this manifestly seems to be fulfilled in the multitude of those who have believed in God through Christ out of the different nations.

The present section some of the Jews interpret of the Babylonian captivity, when the temple was desolate for seventy years, and there were no altar and victims and priesthood, and afterwards under Zerubbabel they returned to their former seats. Others, like us, defer it to the future time; and what is the cause of so great an offense, that they have been abandoned for so long a time, especially since they do not worship idols, they cannot find any other than the killing of the Savior.

For many days the sons of Israel will sit without a king, and without a prince, and without sacrifice, and without altar, and without ephod, and without teraphim. And after this the sons of Israel will return and will seek the Lord their God and David their king; and they will tremble before the Lord and before his goodness in the last of days. LXX: For many days the sons of Israel will sit without a king, without a prince, without sacrifice, without altar, without priesthood, without manifestations, — which in Greek are called δῆλοι —. And after this the sons of Israel will return, and will seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and they will be astonished before the Lord, and at his good things on the last day. For ephod and teraphim the Seventy translated ἱερατείαν, that is, priesthood, and δήλους, that is, manifestations. Now it should be known, as we have often said, that ephod signifies a priestly garment, which in Exodus and Leviticus is called by the LXX ἐπωμὶς, that is, the shoulder-piece, and by Aquila ἐπένδυμα, that is, the over-garment. Teraphim, however, properly means μορφώματα, that is, figures and images, which we can say, in the present passage at least, are the cherubim and seraphim or the other things which were ordered to be made for the adornment of the temple. But since the Seventy translated δήλους, for which Aquila rendered φωτισμούς (illuminations), and these very things are in the λογείῳ, that is, in the rational, we understand this: that in the breast and heart of the high priest there ought to be ἀλήθεια and φωτισμοί, that is, truth and teaching, so that he may not only know the right faith, but may also be able to bring forth with his mouth what he knows. This the apostle Paul also writes to Titus, teaching what kind of man should be ordained bishop: For a bishop must be without crime, as the steward of God; not proud, not quick to anger, not given to wine, not a striker and not greedy for shameful gain; but hospitable, kind, sober, just, holy, continent, embracing the faithful word which is according to doctrine, so that he may be able both to exhort in sound doctrine and to refute those who contradict. Ephod and teraphim we also read of in the book of Judges, which the Levite had made for himself, who afterwards set out with six hundred armed men of the tribe of Dan. From the passion of the Lord the Savior up to the present day, almost the four hundredth year is being completed, and how much time remains until the day of judgment neither the angels know nor the Son. He says that he does not know for this reason, because it is not expedient for us to learn. These, then, are the many days in which the unhappy Synagogue and adulterous woman is fed on barley, and has sat huddled, because she cannot stand with Christ. Without a king, of whom the Father spoke: I have raised up a king with justice. And he himself says in the psalm: But I have been appointed king by him over Zion, his holy mountain. Without a prince: either the Lord the Savior himself, or at least the high priest, of whom it is written: You shall not curse the prince of your people. And without sacrifice, and without altar. For since the temple was overthrown, and Jerusalem was burnt, the Jewish nation can carry on neither sacrifice nor priesthood. And without ephod and without teraphim, that is, the instruments of the priestly dress. Of this king Jacob too speaks in the blessing of the patriarch Judah: A prince shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until he comes for whom it is laid up; and he will be the expectation of the nations. Therefore, after the prince failed from Judah, and the leader from his thighs, and Herod, a foreigner and a proselyte, took the rule, we understand that he has come for whom the kingdom was laid up, and he will be the expectation of the nations.

This is the blindness which has happened in part to Israel, so that the fullness of the Gentiles might come in, and then all Israel would be saved; and after a long time they will return and will seek the Lord their God, and David their king, who was born of the stock of David, and whose name is interpreted strong of hand. For he himself released the captivity of his people, and gave release to those in bonds. And when the sons of Israel see him, who was denied by his own brothers, reigning in the majesty of the Father and in his own, they will tremble and be astonished before the Lord and before his Good One, he who, a good son, was born of a good father; or to the good things of the Lord, of which the saint speaks: I believe I shall see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living; for this land which we sinners inhabit is the land of the dead.

But let us hear what Hosea goes on to say: "And after this the children of Israel shall return and shall seek the Lord their God and David their king; and they shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the last days." You will never find a prophecy plainer than this, for the name King David means Christ, who, as Paul says, "was born according to the flesh of the offspring of David." Further on still, Hosea foretold the resurrection of Christ on the third day, but in the mysterious way that is proper to prophecy. He says, "He shall heal us after two days, and on the third day we shall rise up again." This is the theme underlying the words of Paul: "Therefore if you have risen with Christ, seek the things that are above."
4: Hear the word of the Lord, sons of Israel, for the Lord has a judgment with the inhabitants of the earth. For there is no truth, and there is no mercy, and there is no knowledge of God on the earth; cursing, and lying, and murder, and theft, and adultery have flooded in; and blood has touched blood. LXX: Hear the word of the Lord, sons of Israel, for the Lord has a judgment against the inhabitants of the earth; for there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God upon the earth. Cursing, and lying, and murder, and theft, and adultery have been poured out upon the earth, and they have mingled blood with blood. From the beginning of the prophet up to this place, under the description of a harlot and of an adulteress, after whose most grievous punishments and very long abandonment there comes afterwards a restoration to the former, or to a better, state, the sins of the ten tribes, or of the two, and of all in common, are enumerated. Now the discourse turns again to Israel, that is, to the ten tribes, setting forth that it is not without cause that an angry God threatens and inflicts such grievous punishments; lest perhaps the sentence passed against those who had not sinned should seem to have been passed unjustly, not from the truth of judgment but from the power of God. Hear, says the prophet, the word of the Lord, O sons of Israel; for the Lord wishes to enter into judgment with his people and to set forth the causes of his indignation. There is no truth, and there is no mercy, and there is no knowledge of God on the earth. For neither can truth be sustained without mercy, and mercy without truth makes men negligent; hence the one is mingled with the other, and whoever does not have these will consequently not have the knowledge of God either. But on the contrary, in place of truth there is lying, and in place of mercy cursing, murder, theft, adultery. He did not say "are", but, to show the abundance of the offenses, he added: have overflowed; and in place of the knowledge of God, which is not on the earth, blood has touched blood, or they have mingled blood with blood, so as to add sins to sins and heap new ones upon the old. And rightly are those who are inhabitants of the earth, and not sojourners, summoned to judgment, because from the face of the north evils blaze up upon the inhabitants of the earth. And in the Apocalypse of John woe, woe, woe is pronounced upon the inhabitants of the earth. But whoever can say with the prophet: I am a stranger with you, and a pilgrim, as all my fathers were; and passes through this world as a sojourner and a pilgrim, follows truth and mercy and the knowledge of God, so as not to be overwhelmed by the flood of cursing and of lying, of murder and of theft, and of adultery and of blood.

After Moses, prophets were sent to heal Israel. But in their exercise of healing they deplored the fact that they could not overcome evil, so that one of them says, "The faithful are gone from the earth, among men the upright are no more," and again, "All alike have gone astray; they have become perverse; there is not one who does good, not even one." And again, "Cursing, and theft, and adultery, and killing have overflowed" upon the land. "They sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons." They engaged themselves in auguries and enchantments and divinations; and again, "they fastened their garments with cords and hung veils next to the altar."

Because of this the earth will mourn, and everyone who dwells in it will languish; with the beast of the field and with the bird of the sky; and even the fish of the sea will be gathered up. LXX: Therefore the earth will mourn and will be diminished with all who inhabit it: with the beasts of the field, with the serpents of the earth, and with the fowls of the sky, and the fish of the sea will fail. Because there is no truth, and there is no mercy, and there is no knowledge of God upon the earth; but, over against these, cursing and lying, and murder and theft and adultery have flooded in, and blood has touched blood. Therefore the earth will mourn with its inhabitants, and will languish, so that it has no beasts of the field and birds of the sky, and the fish of the sea will fail. For when the captivity of the ten tribes has come, once the inhabitant has been taken away, the beasts too and the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea will fail, and even the mute elements will feel the wrath of the Lord. Whoever does not believe that this happened to the people of Israel, let him look at Illyricum, let him look at the Thracian provinces, Macedonia and the Pannonias, and all the land that stretches from the Propontis and the Bosphorus to the Julian Alps, and he will find it proved that, together with men, all the living creatures also fail which were formerly nourished by the Creator for the uses of men. But if we wish, as some think, to interpret the beasts as savage men, and the birds of the sky as those who are lifted up into pride and despise all human things, and the fish as those who are irrational, and so dull that they have no understanding at all, and do not see the free air and the sky; then this is the act of a Lord not so much angry as merciful, that the things which are evil should be taken away from the earth.

Nevertheless let no one judge, and let no man be reproved; for your people are like those who contradict the priest; and you will fall today, and the prophet too will fall with you. LXX: So that no one is either judged, or anyone reproved; but my people are like a priest who will be contradicted, and he will be weakened by day, and the prophet too will be weakened with you. According to the Seventy translators, this which we have set down, so that no one is either judged, or anyone reproved, must be fitted to the preceding section. But let us follow the Hebrews. The sons of Israel who dwelt in the land, having been summoned to the judgment of God to hear the causes of the Lord's indignation and to recognize the past sins for which they were to be handed over to their enemies, now, because they persevere in their crimes and despise God with a shameless brow, hear: There is no need for you to come to judgment, to be reproved for your outrages; for you are of such shamelessness that not even when convicted do you have shame and modesty; but you contradict me, as if, like a disciple against his master, the common rabble, which does not have the dignity of the priesthood, were contradicting the priest.

My people are like a priest who is compromised. He has fallen from his previous dignity and does not appear worthy for any reason, just as a priest who falls into controversy would be set aside and dishonored by everyone. "And he will be weak by day." To the greatest extent he will become weak because of the upcoming evils.

By night I have made your mother silent.

My people has fallen silent, because it had no knowledge; because you have rejected knowledge, I too will reject you, so that you may not serve as priest to me; and you have forgotten the law of your God, I too will forget your sons. LXX: I have likened your mother to the night, and my people has been likened to one not having knowledge; because you have rejected knowledge, I too will reject you, so that you may not serve as priest to me; you have forgotten the law of your God, and I too will forget your sons. He calls them mother and sons, not because the mother is one thing and the sons another; but just as the Lord, speaking to the people of the Jews, said: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you, how often I wished to gather your sons, as a hen gathered her chicks under her wings, and you would not? Not that Jerusalem was one thing and her people another; for he was not speaking to the rubble of the city and its timbers and stones apart from the people. So the multitude of the people and the whole crowd of the Hebrew nation to which he speaks is called mother; and the sons are either the individuals of the people, or those scattered through the towns and villages. In the night, then, and in the darkness of captivity and of grief and of pressing distress Israel is handed over, and its people falls silent in eternal silence; because it did not have knowledge of the law, nor did it keep the commandments of God, and it received back what it had done. For she herself rejected the law of God, and therefore lost the priesthood forever, worshiping the golden calves in Dan and Bethel; and because she forgot the law of God and gave herself over wholly as a slave to Egyptian idols, therefore the Lord too will forget her sons, handing them over to eternal captivity: For whoever does not know will not be known; and in the psalms we read: They did not know, nor did they understand; they walk in darkness. All the things that are said to the ten tribes we can refer to the heretics, who have left the kingdom of David and Jerusalem, that is, Christ and the Church; and therefore they are covered with eternal night, and do not have the knowledge of God, and are rejected by the Lord, so that they may not serve as priests to him, and he never remembers the sons whom they have begotten, because they have become alien sons to him.

And because you are such, therefore today you fall, that is, you are led into captivity, and you lose the kingdom of Israel. Now as for his saying: today, it either signifies the present time, or that you will be led into captivity not by fraud and ambush but in broad daylight; and so great will be your weakness that even the prophets, who used to prophesy a lie to you, will fall with you and experience captivity. Here we ought to understand by the prophets either the false prophets, or at least every prophetic grace. For as long as the ten tribes had not been taken captive, they had both the prophet Elijah and Elisha, and the other sons of the prophets, who prophesied in Samaria. Hence also the prophet Amos, who was of the tribe of Judah and of the little village of Tekoa, is compelled to return to his own country, so as not to prophesy in a foreign kingdom and in Samaria.

Of the ones who first made use of false predictions to deceive you, most will also themselves become weak because of the calamity that holds them back. As if they were wrapped up in some kind of night darkness, they see the pursuit of deceit, which was useless for them.

For us too, you see, once the night of this age is done, there will be a resurrection of the flesh for the kingdom; it's the model or sample of this that has already occurred in our head. That, indeed, is why the Lord wished to rise again at night; because, in the apostle's words, "God, who commanded the light to shine out of the darkness, has shone in our hearts." So the Lord represented light shining out of darkness by being born at night and also by rising at night. Light out of darkness, in fact, is Christ out of the Jews, to whom it was said, "I have likened your mother to night." But in that nation, as it were in that night, the virgin Mary was not night but somehow or other a star of the night; which is why a star also signaled her childbearing, guiding a far distant night, that is the magi from the east, to worship the light. Thus in them too would be realized the command to "the light to shine out of darkness."

For He even said by one of the holy prophets to the people of the Jews, "I have compared your mother to the night: My people is like to him that has no knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from being My priest: and because you have forgotten the law of your God, I will also forget your sons." Observe therefore that He compares Jerusalem to the night; for the darkness of ignorance veiled the heart of the Jews, and blinded their eyes: and for this reason they were given over to destruction and slaughter.
Commentary on the Gospel of Luke
One says that Israel will be weak not forever but for days. For it has been reserved for her a time of salvation and a return to faith.

Because the ecclesiastical hierarchy is founded upon Scripture, which is compared to the water of the sea, therefore sentence has been passed against those who do not possess this knowledge. In Hosea: "Because you have rejected knowledge, I will reject you, that you shall not minister to me as priest." He who knows nothing of governance is driven from the helm of the ship and from the rule of the city. If the foundations of the Church consist in the knowledge of sacred Scripture, therefore he who does not know sacred Scripture must be driven from ecclesiastical office and dignity. If a blind man wished to lead another, it would be the greatest folly. A helmsman is not to be chosen by lot or by friendship. And it should be known that knowledge is rejected when a man does not take care to learn it.

Concerning the heretics the understanding is easy: that the more numerous they are, the more they sin against God and glory in their peoples; and therefore they deceive the unhappy, so as to eat the sins of the people, and through sweet words to devour the houses of widows. For when they see some people sinning, they say: God seeks nothing else but the truth of faith; if you guard it, he does not care what you do. For by saying these things they lift up their souls in their iniquities, so that they not only do not repent nor are humbled, but rejoice in their crimes and walk with neck held high. Hence both the people and the priest, both those who have been taught and those who taught, will be bound by an equal judgment.

According to their multitude, so have they sinned against me; I will change their glory into disgrace, and they will eat the sins of my people, and will lift up their souls to their iniquities; and it will be, as the people, so the priest; and I will visit upon him his ways, and I will repay him his thoughts. LXX: According to their multitude, so have they sinned against me; I will turn their glory into disgrace; they will eat the sins of my people, and in their iniquities they will take their souls, and it will be, as the people, so also the priest; and I will avenge upon him his ways, and I will repay him his thoughts. As many men as Israel had, so many altars did it build to demons, in whose victims it sinned against me. Therefore their glory, in which they gloried for themselves and preferred idols to God, I will change into disgrace, so that both priests and peoples are taken captive.

The text wants you to make a more daring assertion if your hearing will still follow. What is the "sacrifice" that is offered "for sin" and is "very holy" except "the only begotten Son of God," Jesus Christ my Lord? He alone is the "sacrifice for sins," and he is "a very holy offering." But since it added that "the priest who offers it will eat it," it seems to be hard to understand. For that which it says must be eaten seems to be referring to the sin, just as in another place the prophet says concerning the priests that "they will eat the sins of my people." This also shows that the priest ought to eat the sin of the one who is offering. We frequently show from holy Scripture that Christ is also the sacrifice that is offered for the sin of the world and the priest who brings the offering.

For indeed the priests eat the sins of my people, the priests of whom it is written: Who devour my people as a meal of bread. And they eat the sins of my people for this reason, that they consent to the crimes of those who offend; for when they have seen them sinning, they not only do not reprove them, but praise and extol them, and proclaim them blessed. Of these Isaiah too speaks: My people, those who call you blessed lead you astray, and trip up the paths of your feet. Of these the psalmist also cries out: For the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul, and the unjust man is blessed.

They used to sacrifice goats for sin; for this reason the sacrifice was called sin. By offering a goat on the altar, the priests at the right time used to bring the intestines and the lard, and they ate the rest. This was ordered by the divine law. … "They eat the sins of my people" means they eat the offerings brought for sins.

But we must remember without ceasing what is written about certain ones: They shall eat the sins of my people. Why are they said to eat the sins of the people, unless because they encourage the sins of transgressors, lest they lose their temporal payments? But we also who live from the offerings of the faithful, which they offered for their sins, if we eat and remain silent, we without doubt eat their sins. Let us consider, therefore, what a crime it is before God to eat the price of sins and to do nothing against sins by preaching.

Hence the people and the priest alike will bear the sentence of an indignant God; because he will visit not only their works, which are called ways, in which they walk, but also the thoughts with which they deliberated in order to do such things. For not only the work, but also the thought of an evil work will pay the penalty.

Seemingly he calls "ways" the walking in works and "counsels" the faults from outrageous thoughts. Then, he says, she [Israel] did not go rightly, having turned aside from the straight road. As if marching the footpath of all profanity, they devised the most shameful and absurd things, dishonoring the God of all while turning toward idolatry.

When, he says, the avenging judgment begins to work, these measures of griefs that they [Israel] made in sins will be filled, so that they may experience in punishments what they have achieved in desires.

We seek no gain of souls, we attend daily to our own pursuits, we desire earthly things, we eagerly chase human glory with intent mind. And because by the very fact that we are placed over others, we have greater license to do whatever we wish, we turn the ministry of the blessing we received into an instrument of ambition; we abandon God's cause, we attend to earthly business; we receive a place of holiness, and we are entangled in earthly activities. What is written has surely been fulfilled in us: "And it shall be, as with the people, so with the priest." For the priest does not differ from the people when by no merit of his own does he transcend the common conduct.

The ten tribes too played the harlot with the idols of Jeroboam son of Nebat; and they forsook their God, not keeping what he had commanded when he said: You shall worship the Lord your God and serve him alone, but this is to be read ἐμφατικῶς (emphatically): Fornication and wine and drunkenness take away the heart. For just as wine and drunkenness make him who has drunk no longer master of his mind, so fornication and pleasure pervert the sense and weaken the spirit, and make of a rational man a brute animal, so that he pursues eating-houses and brothels and the dens of lusts. And when the heart has thus been moved from its place, it thinks wood and stones are gods and worships the works of its own hands.

The heretics are never satisfied with their error, nor do they cease from the foulness of fornication, and daily, by not keeping the law and the holy Scriptures, they forsake the Lord, they rave and become drunk; and having lost the judgment of the mind, they worship idols which they have fashioned from their own heart, and are possessed by the spirit of fornication.

And they will eat and will not be satisfied; they have played the harlot and have not ceased, since they have forsaken the Lord in not observing; fornication and wine and drunkenness take away the heart. My people has inquired of its wood, and its staff has declared to it. For the spirit of fornications deceives them, and they have played the harlot away from their God. LXX: And they will eat and will not be filled; they have played the harlot and will not be set straight, because they have forsaken the Lord, so as not to observe; the heart of my people has taken up fornication and wine and drunkenness; they inquired by auguries, and by their rods they made announcement to it; for they have been led astray by a spirit of fornication and have played the harlot away from their God. Pleasure is insatiable, and the more of it is taken, the more hunger it creates in those who use it. On the contrary, blessed are those who hunger and thirst for justice, for they shall be satisfied. As justice satisfies, so iniquity, having no substance, mocks with deceit those who eat empty things, and leaves the bellies of those who devour it empty. They have played the harlot and have not ceased. Their strength fails in fornication, and the desire to fornicate does not rest.

A remnant from Israel has been preserved. Since the judgment does not go entirely to the priest, he adds, "They eat, but they are not satisfied." This means either emigration and captivity for those leaders of Israel or, because of Christ, desolation of Judea by the hands of Romans.… For among those Israelites brought then by Shalmaneser and Tiglath-pileser III to Assyria and Media, very few could offer to the priests the things prescribed by the law.

"They kept the whoredom" means that they [Israel's leaders] got ready to preserve the error for those who were under their authority. Yet they should rather have removed and thrown it from their midst. For it is the vigilance of the teachers which should eagerly remove what hurts the people and turn down without delay what is hateful to God. By refusing to do this, they allow the works of error to stay somehow and to keep. Yet they confirm rather the contrary, when the minds of those who teach receive nothing but wine and drunkenness. For how will the disciples keep vigil, and how will they be able to point the eye of the understanding to God in nature and in truth, if the instructors and the teachers of useful things will still encourage them to err?

Anthony then asked, "Who are you who say such things to me? And at once he [the demonic voice] uttered a contemptible speech: 'I am a lover of fornication; I have undertaken to ensnare the young and to entice them to it, and I am called the spirit of fornication. How many I have deceived who wished to be chaste! How many who practiced self-restraint have I by my seductions persuaded to change! I am he on whose account the prophet reproaches the fallen, saying, "You have been deceived by the spirit of fornication," for through me they were tripped up. I am he who often troubled you but whom you as often overthrew.' "

The unclean spirit before had been in the synagogue and had led them into idolatry. Of him it is written, "The spirit of harlotry has led them astray." The spirit had gone out of a man and was roaming in the dry places in search of a resting place and could find none. He took with him seven other demons and returned to his former dwelling place. All these spirits were in the synagogue and could not bear the presence of the Savior. Indeed, "what harmony is there between Christ and Belial?" Christ and Belial could not abide in the same assembly. "Now in their synagogue there was a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out, saying, 'What have we to do with you?' " Who is asking, "What have we to do with you?" He is only one, but he cries out the recognition of many. He is aware that in his own defeat, his devils have been vanquished with him.

Hence the prophet too, as if astonished and full of wonder, declares: My people, which was once called by my name, has inquired of wood and of rods; a kind of divination which the Greeks call ῥαβδομαντείαν (divination by rods). Hence we also read in Ezekiel that Nebuchadnezzar mixed his rods against Ammon and Jerusalem, and the rod came out against Jerusalem; and the cause of this madness is the spirit of fornication, which deceived them, so that they played the harlot away from their God. Now fornication signifies idolatry, according to what we read in Jeremiah: And they committed adultery with wood and stone, and I said: After they have played the harlot with all these, return to me; and she did not return with her whole heart, but in falsehood. And again: You have forsaken me and said: I will go upon every high hill, and I will pour myself out in my fornication under every leafy tree. And in the psalm it is said: You have destroyed all who play the harlot away from you. For the beginning of fornication is the invention of idols.

It is a grave displeasure, after you have sinned, not to merit the wrath of the Lord. Israel had played the harlot away from the Lord his God and been led astray by a spirit of fornication; therefore his daughters and brides also play the harlot and are left in their crime without any punishment, so that what the sons and the wife had done to their true parent and husband, they may feel in their own children and wives, and from their own pain understand the pain of God, who is so angry that he does not strike the offenders at all. The Apostle too, writing to the Romans, testifies to this in mystical speech: For, saying that they were wise, they became fools; and they changed the glory of the incorruptible God into the likeness of the image of corruptible man, and of birds, and of four-footed beasts, and of serpents. And because they had played the harlot with idols, they are struck with such a sentence: For this reason God gave them up to the desires of their heart, to uncleanness, so that they dishonor their bodies among themselves, who exchanged the truth of God for a lie; and they worshipped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. But that we may know that visitation is brought by God, as upon the wounded and the sick, for this purpose, that as by cautery and most bitter potions they may recover health and be free of diseases, let us hear God speaking through the prophet: I will visit their iniquities with the rod, and their sins with stripes; but my mercy I will not scatter from him. He, therefore, who is loved is corrected; he who is neglected is left to his sins. And so great was the number of fornicators in Israel that the vengeance was one that despaired of amendment. For what is more shameful than for men to be joined to the worship of harlots, and with the effeminate to offer the victims of their own lust? But what he adds: the people that does not understand will be beaten; for which the Seventy translated: And the people that understands clung to the harlot; this signifies that Israel is beaten in captivity and afflicted with various blows, so that through pain it may receive discipline. Concerning the heretics the understanding is easy: their daughters and brides play the harlot, that is, the souls which they have begotten in error and betrothed to their own dogmas. Men of this kind are unworthy of God's correction, since all their worship is fornication, and the shameful are mingled with the shameful; and therefore they will be beaten, so that at some time through blows they may understand what God they should seek. When you see a sinner abounding in riches, boasting of his power, rejoicing in health, delighting in his wife, surrounded by a crown of children, and that which is written being fulfilled: They are not in the labor of men, and with men they will not be scourged, say that in him the prophet's threat has been fulfilled: I will not visit upon your daughters when they have played the harlot and upon your brides when they have committed adultery.

On the tops of the mountains they sacrificed, and on the hills they burned incense; under the oak and the poplar and the terebinth, because its shade was good. LXX: On the summit of the mountains they sacrificed, and on the hills they offered victims; under the oak and the poplar and the shady trees, because the shelter was good. In the law it is commanded that no sacrifice be made to the Lord except in the place which the Lord God shall choose; and that a grove and trees not be planted beside the altar, lest, namely, a promiscuous and pleasure-loving religion overturn the austerity of the one and true religion. On the contrary, Israel sacrificed on the mountains and burned incense on the hills, loving the high places of the earth because it had forsaken God on high, and seeking the shade it had lost the truth. This is what we read of the several kings: Nevertheless he did not take away the high places; the people still offered victims and sacrificed on the high places, which in Hebrew is called bama. The heretics promise themselves loftiness of dogmas, and they sacrifice under the oak and the poplar and the terebinth, unfruitful trees, which have not the fig and the vine under which the saint is said to rest. But at times they take up for themselves the terebinth, which according to Isaiah has no leaves, so that they may seem to imitate the example of Abraham.

But do you wish to hear the terrible voice of an indignant God? Hear what he says through the prophet: when he had enumerated the many wicked things which the people had committed, he adds also these: "and for this reason" he says "I will not visit upon your daughters when they fornicate, nor upon your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery". This is the terrible thing, this the extremity: when we are no longer rebuked for our sins, when we are no longer corrected when we transgress. For then, when we have exceeded the measure of sinning, the "jealous God" turns his jealousy away from us, as he said above: "for my jealousy shall be taken away from you, and I will be angry over you no more". So much concerning that which was said: "a jealous God".

Therefore your daughters will play the harlot, and your brides will be adulteresses.

I will not visit upon your daughters when they have played the harlot, and upon your brides when they have committed adultery; since they themselves consorted with harlots and sacrificed with the effeminate; and the people that does not understand will be beaten. LXX: Therefore your daughters will play the harlot and your brides will commit adultery, and I will not visit upon your daughters when they have played the harlot and upon your brides when they have committed adultery; because they themselves also mingled with harlots and offered victims with the initiated; and the people that understands clung to the harlot. The word cadesoth, which Aquila translated ἐνηλλαγμένων, Symmachus ἑταιρίδων, the Seventy τετελεσμένων, Theodotion κεχωρισμένων, we have rendered 'effeminate', so as to lay open the sense of the word to the ears of our own people. These are they who today at Rome, serving the mother not of the gods but of demons, are called Galli, because the Romans, in honor of Attis — whom the harlot goddess had made a eunuch —, made over men of this nation, cut off from lust, as her priests. And the men of the nation of the Gauls are unmanned for this reason: that those who had captured the city of Rome may be struck with this disgrace.
